articles.title: Así se puede ‘reparar’ un cerebro adicto a las pantallas para que vuelva a concentrarse
articles.text:
Reparar un cerebro adicto a las pantallas para que vuelva a sostener la concentración es posible, según coinciden varios especialistas en neurociencia y psicología cognitiva.
El punto de partida es una cifra que preocupa a los investigadores: el tiempo promedio que una persona dedica a una tarea frente a una pantalla antes de cambiar de actividad cayó de dos minutos y medio en 2004 a apenas 47 segundos en la actualidad.
PUBLICIDAD
El dato surge de los estudios de Gloria Mark, profesora de Informática en la Universidad de California en Irvine, quien mide este fenómeno desde hace dos décadas.
Por qué las pantallas fragmentan la atención
El cerebro humano no procesa la información de forma continua, sino mediante filtros que priorizan ciertos estímulos y suprimen otros. Ese mecanismo recibe el nombre de atención.
“Aspectos de la atención a veces se comparan con un foco que escanea continuamente el entorno y se detiene para iluminar la información importante”, señaló Ian Fiebelkorn, profesor asociado de Neurociencia en el Instituto Del Monte para la Neurociencia de la Universidad de Rochester.
Según sus investigaciones, ese foco atencional no solo se atenúa en los períodos largos que solemos llamar “capacidad de atención”, sino también en una escala de tiempo mucho más veloz. Entre cuatro y seis veces por segundo existe una ventana en la que una distracción puede desviar el foco de lo que se intenta hacer.
PUBLICIDAD
Las pantallas explotan esas ventanas de vulnerabilidad. Las aplicaciones combinan sonidos y vibraciones para mantener un flujo constante de sensaciones, de manera que el cerebro asocia el cambio de tarea con una recompensa inmediata. Ese circuito de estímulo y premio refuerza el hábito de saltar de una actividad a otra.
El costo de saltar entre tareas y pantallas
Cambiar de actividad todo el tiempo no es gratuito para el organismo. Mark encontró una correlación directa entre la frecuencia con la que una persona cambia de foco y sus niveles de estrés, medidos con monitores de frecuencia cardíaca.
“Cuanto más rápido ocurre el cambio de atención, el estrés aumenta”, indicó la investigadora, quien agregó que décadas de estudios de laboratorio muestran que la multitarea eleva la presión arterial y otros marcadores fisiológicos de tensión.
PUBLICIDAD
A ese desgaste se suma lo que Mark denomina “costo de cambio”: cada vez que se interrumpe una tarea para pasar a otra, el cerebro necesita tiempo para reorientarse y recordar en qué punto se había quedado. Ese proceso consume recursos mentales adicionales, incrementa los errores y ralentiza el desempeño, algo documentado en estudios con médicos, enfermeros y pilotos.
No todos los cambios de actividad son perjudiciales. Tomar una pausa después de terminar una sección de trabajo, en lo que Mark llama un “punto de quiebre” natural, permite recuperar energía sin generar el mismo desgaste que una interrupción abrupta en medio de una tarea.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo entrenar de nuevo la concentración
La primera recomendación de los especialistas apunta a reducir las distracciones antes de que aparezcan. “La mejor manera de evitar cambios frecuentes del foco atencional es eliminar las distracciones potenciales”, afirmó Fiebelkorn, quien sugiere apagar el celular o dejarlo en otra habitación durante el estudio o el trabajo, y desconectar internet si la tarea puede hacerse sin conexión.
Otra estrategia consiste en disminuir el atractivo visual del teléfono. Apagar la vibración, el sonido y el color de la pantalla desde los ajustes reduce los estímulos que recibe el cerebro y, con el tiempo, baja las ganas de revisar el dispositivo.
PUBLICIDAD
Programar descansos estructurados también ayuda a reducir la incertidumbre que agota al cerebro. Comenzar con bloques breves de concentración, de uno a tres minutos, e ir aumentando la duración de forma progresiva permite entrenar la capacidad de sostener el foco sin que una distracción arruine el intento.
Fiebelkorn coincide en la importancia de este punto: “El cerebro se cansa después de concentrarse durante mucho tiempo. Para ayudar a evitar esta fatiga, se pueden programar pausas breves dentro de una sesión de estudio o trabajo”.
Finalmente, ambos especialistas remarcan que concentrarse en una sola tarea a la vez es más eficaz que intentar abarcar varias. “Si tienes una tarea importante, dale toda tu atención y completala antes de pasar a la siguiente”, propuso Fiebelkorn.
PUBLICIDAD
Mark agrega que mantener el “tanque” de recursos mentales lleno, con buen descanso nocturno, es determinante para poder enfocarse: la falta de sueño acumulada, o “deuda de sueño”, se asocia directamente con lapsos de atención más cortos y con la tendencia a refugiarse en actividades livianas, como las redes sociales, en lugar de tareas que exigen esfuerzo.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: New PS5 Relapse jailbreak enables homebrew and Switch emulation but is hamstrung by rapidly-changing firmware revisions — jailbreak unlocks firmware 13.60, but newer games already demand firmware 14.00
articles.text:
New PS5 Relapse jailbreak enables homebrew and Switch emulation but is hamstrung by rapidly-changing firmware revisions — jailbreak unlocks firmware 13.60, but newer games already demand firmware 14.00
Some games may require an unsupported version of the PS5 firmware, including the new Wolverine title.
A new PS5 jailbreak has been released with support for all PlayStation 5 consoles running firmware 7.00 through 13.60, meaning all consoles that haven't been updated within the last week or so are compatible. That includes the latest PS5 Pro console, too.
The new jailbreak, called Relapse, uses browser and kernel exploits to unlock kernel read and write access, including support for additional payloads like the homebrew enabler etaHEN.
However, while support for consoles all the way up to firmware 13.60 opens the door to more jailbreakers than ever before, the free-for-all might be short-lived. As VideoCardz reports, some games are already requiring the latest 14.00 firmware in order to download updates.
One example is the new Marvel's Wolverine game, with gamers reporting that the disc-based version requires PS5 firmware version 13.40. Downloading the latest 1.001.005 game update bumps the required firmware to version 13.60, which shouldn't be a problem for the Relapse jailbreak. But the fly in the ointment appears to be the digital version of the game. Some gamers have reported that the same update for the digital version of the game requires firmware version 14.00, pushing the PS5 beyond the firmware supported by Relapse.
This news leaves PS5 jailbreakers with a familiar Catch-22 situation. Some games, especially future releases, may require a newer version of the PS5 firmware in order to run. But installing those newer PS5 firmwares will break the jailbreak, giving gamers a decision to make — do they want to play the latest games or maintain their jailbreak?
Marvel's Wolverine aside, there are a number of reasons that gamers may wish to jailbreak their PS5 or PS5 Pro consoles. Doing so bypasses Sony's software restrictions, giving gamers the chance to install and run non-standard software and games. That can include pirated titles, of course, but it also means that emulators, including one for Nintendo Switch games, and mods can be used on a PlayStation. Naturally, those who choose to do this accept the inherent risks involved and do so at their own risk.
More information about Relapse can be found on the jailbreak's GitHub page.

articles.title: Synopsys and Amazon Announce Strategic, Multi-year IP Agreement for Custom Silicon
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 30th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Synopsys and Amazon Announce Strategic, Multi-year IP Agreement for Custom Silicon
Synopsys, Inc. (Nasdaq: SNPS) today announced a strategic agreement with Amazon to accelerate Amazon's custom silicon innovation and advance the development of increasingly complex AI-powered products and cloud infrastructure. The multi-year agreement marks the expansion of Synopsys' silicon IP business to serve increasing demand for application-optimized IP with Amazon as its lead customer.
Amazon continues to build on its leadership and longstanding investment in a broad portfolio of purpose-built chips, including Nitro for cloud security, network and storage, Graviton for general-purpose computing, and Trainium for AI training and inference workloads. Building on more than 15 years of collaboration, the agreement expands Amazon's use of Synopsys' IP to include application-optimized silicon IP. The agreement also expands Amazon's use of Synopsys EDA, simulation and analysis (S&A), and agentic AI technologies. Synopsys and Amazon will work to accelerate multiphysics solutions on Trainium and Graviton.In addition, the companies plan to collaborate on applying AI across silicon-to-system engineering workflows. This includes deploying Synopsys' AI-powered EDA, physics-based simulation and agentic AI solutions, as well as developing custom agentic AI capabilities to help Amazon's engineering teams design, analyze, optimize, and validate complex chips and systems more efficiently.
Peter DeSantis, SVP, foundational AI, custom silicon, quantum computing at Amazon"Amazon has invested in custom silicon for more than a decade, and it has fundamentally changed what's possible for AWS and our customers. From Graviton to Trainium, purpose-built chips deliver better performance at lower cost because they're designed for exactly what customers need. As our chip designs grow more ambitious and AI reshapes the engineering process itself, Synopsys helps us move faster across the design cycle, helping us deliver more capable, efficient computing for customers worldwide."
To accelerate its own IP and EDA tools development, Synopsys is adopting Amazon EC2 and cloud storage services, as well as Amazon Bedrock to build and deploy AI applications and agents to help innovate faster and scale its product offerings.
Sassine Ghazi, president and CEO of Synopsys"Special purpose silicon is at the heart of AWS innovation. As we expand into application-optimized IP solutions, we're proud to have Amazon as our lead customer for this next phase of growth. More broadly, by combining Amazon's leadership in AI infrastructure and custom silicon with Synopsys' leadership in silicon IP, EDA and Multiphysics solutions, we can dramatically increase the productivity of our teams and shape the future of AI-native engineering."

articles.title: Microsoft melhora ainda mais a integração entre Linux e Windows • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Microsoft melhora ainda mais a integração entre Linux e Windows
Microsoft liberou oficialmente o WSL Containers (WSLC), trazendo suporte nativo a contêineres no Linux executado via Windows 11.
A Microsoft acaba de dar um reforço e tanto na integração do Windows 11 com o ecossistema do Linux. Isso porque a companhia liberou oficialmente o suporte a contêineres no Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL), recurso interessante principalmente para desenvolvedores.
Se você está “boiando” no assunto, aqui vai uma rápida explicação: o WSL é uma ferramenta que executa determinadas distribuições Linux em ambiente Windows, dispensando o usuário de rodar máquinas virtuais ou de depender de dual boot para esse fim em determinados cenários. O WSL foi introduzido no Windows 10 e vem sendo melhorado significativamente no Windows 11.
Pois bem, o suporte a contêineres é uma dessas melhorias. Entenda um contêiner como um pacote que combina uma aplicação junto com as suas dependências (bibliotecas, arquivos de configuração, módulos, entre outros), de modo a permitir a sua execução padronizada em diferentes ambientes computacionais.
Desenvolvedores, administradores de TI e afins já podiam trabalhar com contêineres no WSL, mas dependiam de soluções de terceiros para isso. Com a atualização do Windows Subsystem for Linux, a própria ferramenta passa a ter suporte nativo para o recurso.
O WSL Containers (WSLC), como é chamado oficialmente, foi anunciado em junho, durante a Build 2026. A ferramenta foi sendo testada e aprimorada para ser liberada massivamente agora, junto com a chegada da versão 26H2 do Windows 11, ainda que ambas as novidades não estejam interligadas (o WSL é focado no Windows 11 atualmente, mas também funciona no Windows 10 e no Windows Server).
O WSL Containers funciona por meio de uma interface de linha de comando (CLI, na sigla em inglês). Eis alguns exemplos, sendo a maioria destacada pela própria Microsoft:
O último comando é o mais importante porque, efetivamente, coloca o WSLC em ação. Para isso, ele depende de alguns parâmetros. Um exemplo simples é o comando abaixo (mostrado também na imagem de abertura deste texto), que ativa um ambiente Ubuntu, o faz exibir a mensagem “Hello, world!” (comando echo) e depois exclui o contêiner (parâmetro –rm):
wslc run --rm ubuntu:latest bash -c "echo Hello, world!"
Um detalhe interessante é que o WSLC também pode ser executado por meio de uma API. Assim, é possível fazer aplicações para Windows executarem contêineres no WSL de modo direto, o que pode ser útil para automação de determinadas tarefas, por exemplo.
Para ter acesso à novidade, basta digitar o comando wsl –update no PowerShell ou Prompt de Comando para atualizar o WSL (é preciso ter a versão 2.9.3 ou superior). Se a ferramenta não estiver instalada, a instale via comando wsl –install.
Há mais instruções sobre como usar o WSLC na documentação oficial.

articles.title: AWS embeds DuckDB in its PostgreSQL DBMS to speed queries of live and historical data - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AWS embeds DuckDB in its PostgreSQL DBMS to speed queries of live and historical data
Amazon Web Services Inc. is adding the ability to query the popular Apache Iceberg data lake directly from its Aurora PostgreSQL database management system, allowing applications to combine live transactions with historical records without copying data or creating extract/transform/load pipelines.
The capability embeds the DuckDB analytical engine inside Aurora PostgreSQL to support data stored in Iceberg and Apache Parquet formats. Customers can use existing PostgreSQL applications, tools and endpoints to query operational records alongside data in Amazon S3, including S3 Tables.
AWS acquired DuckLabs B.V., developer of the popular open-source database, last month.
AWS is positioning the feature as a way to simplify application development and reduce the engineering work needed to maintain data pipelines. Potential uses include real-time dashboards, transactions enriched with historical information and artificial intelligence agents that need access to both current and archived records.
Previously, combining recent transactions in Aurora with historical records in S3 commonly required reverse ETL pipelines. That resulted in duplicated data, additional infrastructure costs and continuing work to keep records synchronized.
“This challenge only grows as you increasingly embed AI agents into your applications, where it is impractical to predict and pre-replicate every dataset an agent might need,” Esra Kayabali, a principal solutions architect at AWS, wrote in an announcement.
DuckDB processes analytical scans within Aurora, avoiding additional network hops for query processing. A single query can access data lake records alongside live operational data, including uncommitted writes. AWS said integration as an example of how it is incorporating the DuckDB engine widely into its services.
The feature also supports external catalogs compatible with the Iceberg Representational State Transfer Catalog specification through federation with the data catalog in the AWS Glue serverless data integration service. Customers register an external catalog with Glue and create foreign tables that reference its data. Applications can then join Aurora records with Iceberg tables registered across multiple catalogs.
To limit the amount of data read, Aurora filters records and selects relevant columns during query execution. It also caches frequently accessed data. Developers can inspect metrics including rows scanned, bytes read from S3 and cache hits.
In a financial example, Kayabali demonstrated a query combining seven days of customer transactions in Aurora with five years of historical transactions stored in a Parquet file in S3. Aurora inferred the historical table’s schema from file metadata, eliminating manual column definitions.
For workloads needing single-digit-millisecond latency, customers can copy selected data lake records into native Aurora tables using standard SQL commands. Read queries can run on the cluster’s writer or a read replica, offloading analytical scans from operational workloads. Commands that materialize data run on the writer.
Customers enable the capability through the aurora_analytics extension and an AWS Identity and Access Management role granting access to S3 and Glue. It supports Aurora PostgreSQL versions 17 and 18, starting with versions 17.11 and 18.6, respectively.
AWS said the feature is available in all commercial AWS regions without an additional feature charge. Customers pay for the incremental Aurora computing resources their queries consume and S3 requests used to read files.

articles.title: Shure Launches Next Generation of the MV6 USB Gaming Microphone
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 30th 2026
	
	
	
	
Shure Launches Next Generation of the MV6 USB Gaming Microphone
Today, Shure announced the launch of the MV6 USB Gaming Microphone Gen 2, including a new white variant, the latest evolution of its digital MOTIV microphone portfolio. Following the success of the original MV6, the MV6 Gen 2 incorporates feedback from gamers, streamers, and creators to deliver a more customizable audio experience while maintaining an accessible price point.
Engineered specifically for PC gaming, streaming and content creation, the MV6 Gen 2 brings Shure's professional broadcast technology to more creators, including those purchasing their first dedicated microphone and looking to elevate their sound beyond a headset.New for Gen 2, the enhanced MV6 gives gamers, streamers, and creators more control over the intelligent processing that made the original so powerful. Built around Shure's Voice Isolation Technology, the mic now adds adjustable Auto Level Mode and an adjustable Real-Time Denoiser to more effectively manage sudden volume changes and background noise during gameplay and streaming. The result is personalized audio that stays clear and consistent, helping users stay focused on their game while providing greater freedom to position the microphone where it works best for their setup and on-camera presence.
T Banks, Product Manager at Shure"Gamers and streamers aren't audio engineers, and they shouldn't have to be to sound great. They whisper during tense strategic moments, shout during victories, and stream from environments ranging from quiet bedrooms to noisy shared spaces. With the MV6 Gen 2, the audio intelligence sits inside the microphone's hardware itself. The mic does the heavy lifting of managing volume spikes and erasing background room noise, directly out-of-the-box."

The MV6 Gen 2 is designed for the realities of gaming, streaming, and content creation, from sudden volume changes and background noise to setups that move across PCs, tablets, and phones. From Play to Everyday. MV6 Gen 2 Does It All.

With Shure's immediately recognizable design and audio quality, the MV6 Gen 2 can take users from late-night Discord raids to morning business presentations. articles.title: Emergence AI to Deploy Neuroformal AI With Fabless Chipmakers - EE Times
articles.text:
Emergence AI said it is moving its neuroformal AI technology into active deployments with fabless semiconductor companies, while integrated device manufacturers (IDMs) among its customers are asking the company to extend the work into the fab.
The startup also targets the data generated during manufacturing to identify early signs of degradation before a problem affects a large number of wafers.
In an interview with EE Times at SEMICON India 2026, Satya Nitta, co-founder and executive chairman of Emergence AI, said, “You cannot make chips any faster, but what you can do is definitely get more chips per wafer yielding with AI.”
Nitta said demand for chips exceeds supply and every fab is running at capacity, so more wafers cannot be pushed through. The way to ease the shortage is to get more chips per wafer yielding, which requires analyzing the data, he said.
Nitta said neuroformal AI pairs the creativity of large language models (LLMs) with the discipline of symbolic AI, an older approach based on formal rules that was “all of AI” before the deep learning era. “Algorithms propose, and symbolic AI verifies,” he said. The aim is to develop AI that gives “provably correct” answers that engineers can depend on for mission-critical problems, because LLMs are probabilistic.
Nitta became executive chairman and chief scientist about a month ago, when Emergence AI appointed Ian Eslick as CEO, according to a LinkedIn post by Nitta. He said he will lead the company’s long-term research agenda, advance neuroformal AI, and deepen key partnerships, while Eslick leads the company through its next stage of commercialization and scale.
Eslick founded Silicon Spice, an MIT spinout that Broadcom acquired for $1.2 billion, and later led major technology initiatives at U.S. Bank and SoFi, according to the post.
Fabless companies and yield analysis
Nitta said Emergence AI started with the fabless part of the semiconductor value chain. Fabless companies design the product but do not control the manufacturing process, he said. They have data on the chip itself, such as functional, parametric, and overall yield, but not on what happens in the fab.
He said the analysis can show whether a yield excursion stems from a process issue in the fab, a design issue, or a test issue. “Wafer and final test issues are not uncommon,” he said. “The probe cards do not make perfect contact. I may have to retest it.”
He said AI agents can analyze this data at scale and remember patterns seen across products. As an example, he described an agent that finds the same pattern across 30% of 1,500 products, with failures in a ring oscillator block, and suggests redesigning that block. “These are the kinds of things that AI agents can do that are beyond human cognitive limits,” he said.
Nitta said the company’s domain-specific agents also carry out root-cause analysis. They have to distinguish a spurious correlation from the actual cause, using an understanding of device physics.
Asked whether the company competes with today’s LLMs and GPTs, Nitta said, “I would not say directly competing. We are saying that the LLMs are necessary but not sufficient.” He also said LLM-based AI is “useful but incomplete for mission-critical problems.”
Physics-driven failures in advanced packaging
Nitta said the company is beginning to move into advanced packaging. Because many packaging technologies are still being developed, he said, the question is less about what went wrong in the process and more about fundamental root causes.
One example is a coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch. “It is much more a physics problem,” he said.
He said AI agents would need to run finite-element and multiscale physics simulations to show, for example, that a liner material and copper are incompatible, or that a glass substrate and copper have a large CTE mismatch, causing things to fall apart in thermal cycling. He said that if the via were redesigned, the aspect ratio changed, or the liner thickness increased, “the process window is more mature.”
Nitta said Emergence AI is in active discussions with several advanced packaging companies that could lead to memoranda of understanding. He said he expects several announcements about these engagements in the next two to three months. The company has no active engagements with semiconductor tooling companies, he said.
Nitta said some of the fabless customers are IDMs, which have “both the fabless component and fabs.” The work starts in the fabless part, he said, and the IDMs are now asking the company to work in the fab. The work in the fab is “still at a very early stage,” he added.
Some of the fabless customers are among the largest companies in the industry but he could not name them on the record.
India: focus, talent, and open-source
In India, the company’s focus is limited to semiconductors, Nitta said. Emergence AI is primarily working post-tape-out and is not currently involved in chip design, though that could change in the future. He said verification is one of the longest steps in chip design and that neuroformal AI can accelerate the process.
The company is also talking with several potential Indian customers, but Nitta said he could not name them. “We are in the middle of several discussions,” he said.
Nitta said Emergence AI intends to grow its talent pool to 500 engineers and R&D scientists within two years. EE Times had earlier reported a timeframe of three to four years.
This summer, the company conducted a summer school on Lean, an open-source programming language and proof assistant, for more than 150 students, under the guidance of professor Siddharth Gadgil, chief scientist of Emergence India Labs and a professor at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), and professor Ilya Sergey at the National University of Singapore. Nitta said talent for this work is scarce, so the company is creating it. The company has identified a group of people to whom it is extending talent retention offers.
Nitta said the company has open-sourced parts of its technology from the beginning and is now open-sourcing some of its Lean work with Gadgil and Emergence India Labs. He said aspects of the neuroformal AI work will also be open-sourced to build a community and widen the pool from which the company recruits.
He pointed to Agent-E, an open-source web navigation system the company released in 2024 that automates complex browser tasks using simple natural language. He described it as “the very first autonomous web agent build that was fully open-source” and “the very first time somebody actually open-sourced a complex hierarchical agentic system.” Agent-E is available on GitHub. Nitta indicated that the neuroformal AI work will follow a similar path.
He added that the semiconductor industry is only beginning to explore what autonomous agents can do. “I am delighted to see that even in India, there is enormous growth and support from the central government,” Nitta said. “But we are just scratching the surface.”

articles.title: Un estudio detectó que casi todas las apps para autos envían datos privados a Google, Meta y Microsoft
articles.text:
Una investigación de la Universidad de Northeastern, realizada junto con Consumer Reports, encontró que veintiocho de treinta aplicaciones de autos conectados envían datos a por lo menos una empresa externa de publicidad o análisis, y siete de ellas remiten además información que identifica al conductor.
Los investigadores probaron 21 vehículos de 17 marcas, entre ellas Tesla, Toyota, Honda, Cadillac, Chevrolet, Ford, Lucid y Rivian, junto con las 30 aplicaciones complementarias que los acompañan. El objetivo era rastrear con precisión qué datos salen del auto y hacia qué compañías viajan.
PUBLICIDAD
Para lograrlo, encerraron los autos en una carpa Faraday, una estructura que bloquea las señales electromagnéticas, en el centro de pruebas de Consumer Reports en Connecticut. Así pudieron aislar el tráfico de wifi del vehículo y compararlo con el que generaban las aplicaciones móviles asociadas.
Qué datos viajan y a quién
Entre los principales receptores de esa información aparecen Alphabet (la empresa dueña de Google), Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Pinterest, Snap y Reddit, según el informe publicado por Consumer Reports.
Siete aplicaciones enviaron datos que permiten identificar directamente al dueño del vehículo: su nombre, el número de identificación del vehículo (VIN) o su ubicación geográfica precisa. Las de las marcas de General Motors, como myCadillac, myChevrolet, myBuick y myGMC, junto con HondaLink, MyNissan y Lincoln, compartieron el VIN combinado con un correo electrónico o una ubicación.
PUBLICIDAD
Combinar el VIN con otro identificador personal les permite a las empresas de publicidad vincular al dueño del auto con perfiles de consumo ya armados por corredores de datos, que después se venden a bancos, aseguradoras, farmacéuticas y prestamistas.
“Sepan o no los consumidores, las grandes tecnológicas están metidas en los autos que manejamos”, dijo Nicole Zagson, candidata a doctora en ciberseguridad en Northeastern y coautora del estudio.
Su colega Sarah Elizabeth Gillespie fue más directa todavía: “No parece que un cliente pueda comprar un auto nuevo que no lo rastree”, afirmó, según recogió Consumer Reports.
Cuando el auto se suma al teléfono
El estudio también detectó que emparejar la aplicación del celular con el vehículo duplicaba, en promedio, la cantidad de empresas de publicidad y rastreo que recibían datos del conductor, de acuerdo con la cobertura de TechCrunch sobre la investigación.
PUBLICIDAD
Los modelos que contactaron al mayor número de compañías externas fueron el Cadillac Lyriq, el Chevrolet Blazer, el Lucid Air y los Tesla Model 3 y Cybertruck. Entre las aplicaciones, las de BMW, las marcas de General Motors y Toyota fueron las que se comunicaron con más terceros.
Al ser consultadas, todas las automotrices salvo Honda le trasladaron la responsabilidad al consumidor, según los investigadores. Honda, en cambio, le ordenó a su proveedor Amplitude que borrara todos los datos de ubicación que había recibido y que dejara de enviarlos.
Varias marcas explicaron que algunos enlaces dentro de sus aplicaciones llevan a páginas externas, donde pueden insertarse cookies y píxeles que recolectan datos sin que el conductor lo sepa. Los investigadores señalaron que esto ocurrió sin ningún aviso previo.
PUBLICIDAD
El informe completo, titulado Automatic Transmission: An Empirical Study of Data Privacy in the Connected Vehicle Ecosystem, se publicará esta semana en el sitio de la Universidad de Northeastern.

articles.title: Motorola Razr 60 atinge menor preço dos últimos meses em oferta na Amazon • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Motorola Razr 60 atinge menor preço dos últimos meses em oferta na Amazon
Razr 60 (256 GB) tem mais RAM física e as mesmas telas do Razr 70; dobrável da Motorola registra desconto de 46% e um dos menores preços recentes em oferta no Pix
O Motorola Razr 60 de 256 GB está saindo por apenas R$ 2.969 no Pix na Amazon. O celular dobrável da Motorola, que traz as mesmas telas do novo Razr 70, alcança o menor preço desde julho de 2026, segundo o histórico da plataforma de monitoramento Zoom, com desconto de 46% sobre o original de R$ 5.499.
O Razr 60 traz as mesmas telas do novo Razr 70: interna dobrável é uma POLED de 6,9″ com taxa de 120 Hz e brilho de até 3.000 nits, que reproduz cores excelentes com alta fluidez nas transições, além de visibilidade garantida em qualquer lugar. A externa POLED de 3,6″ suporta Always-On e ações rápidas.
Seu chip MediaTek Dimensity 7400X e os 12 GB de RAM física suportam multitarefa e apps pesados, enquanto o Razr 70 possui apenas 8 GB. Os 256 GB de armazenamento permitem guardar uma quantidade adequada de vídeos e fotos.
O kit de câmeras é formado por uma wide de 50 MP com OIS e uma ultrawide de 13 MP, que captam belas cenas ao ar livre, e uma frontal de 32 MP que tira ótimas selfies em alta resolução. Todas filmam em 4K.
O copo de alumínio com dobradiças de titânio do Razr 60 é reforçado pelo vidro Gorilla Glass Victus sobre a tela externa, resistente contra pancadas e quedas. A certificação IP48 confere proteção contra poeira moderada e mergulhos acidentais.
Sua bateria de 4.500 mAh suporta carregamento rápido de 30 W. Segundo a fabricante, ela permite ao gadget receber uma carga para 12 horas de uso em apenas 15 minutos, um excelente recurso para quem não quer se preocupar com carregadores e tomadas.
O Motorola Razr 60 de 256 GB (apenas R$ 2.969 no Pix) foi atualizado para o Android 16 e deve receber mais dois updates do sistema operacional. O celular conversa com redes 5G, Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.4 e NFC.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: Brosse à dents Dyson à 479€ : on sait enfin ce qui a provoqué le couac industriel
articles.text:
Retirée de la vente en France dix jours seulement après son lancement, une partie des CameraJet souffre d’un défaut de fabrication pouvant laisser passer de l’eau dans l’appareil. Dyson dit avoir identifié le problème, mais doit désormais rassurer les premiers acheteurs.
Dix jours auront suffi pour transformer un lancement surmédiatisé en sérieux couac industriel. Présentée le 1er septembre à 479 euros, la brosse à dents connectée Dyson CameraJet a vu sa commercialisation suspendue en France dès le 11 septembre. Après avoir évoqué des tensions sur les stocks, la marque avait fini par reconnaître l’existence d’un composant défectueux. Elle précise désormais l’origine du problème.
Une fuite provoquée par un défaut de fabrication
Dans une déclaration transmise à Allure, Dyson met en cause un lot de production de tubes utilisés par le jet interdentaire. Un problème survenu lors de leur fabrication aurait créé un risque d’infiltration d’eau susceptible d’altérer le fonctionnement de certains appareils.
La marque affirme avoir isolé les produits concernés, repris la production à plein régime et commencé à expédier des appareils à ses distributeurs. Elle ne donne toutefois aucune date précise pour leur retour en rayon en France.
Sauf qu'on ne comprend pas comment un problème aussi gênant a pu passer entre les mailles du contrôle qualité. Kyle Wiens, patron d’iFixit, avançait auparavant auprès de Wired plusieurs scénarios possibles, notamment des pièces mal ajustées ou une colle ayant mal polymérisé.
Dans ce dernier cas, un produit peut parfaitement fonctionner au moment des tests, puis se dégrader sous l’effet de la chaleur ou de l’humidité pendant le transport. Dyson n’a toutefois pas confirmé l’une ou l’autre de ces hypothèses.
Des premiers acheteurs à rassurer
Plusieurs propriétaires ont signalé de l’eau à proximité de la batterie, des messages de surchauffe ou des appareils devenus inutilisables peu après leur achat. Ces témoignages ne permettent pas de mesurer l’ampleur exacte du problème et Dyson indique qu’aucun rappel général n’est organisé à ce stade, même si certains confrères ont été surpris de voir le géant anglais récupérer leurs exemplaires de test.
Dans ce genre de situation, en cas de fuite ou d’alerte de température, le plus prudent reste évidemment de cesser d’utiliser la CameraJet et de ne pas la remettre en charge avant d’avoir contacté le vendeur ou le SAV Dyson. Mieux vaut également conserver sa preuve d’achat et le numéro de série de l’appareil.
Des consignes de reprise et de remboursement ont circulé chez certains distributeurs, mais leurs modalités peuvent varier. Pour un appareil acheté directement auprès de Dyson, la marque demande de contacter son service consommateurs.
Pour Dyson, l’affaire tombe particulièrement mal. La CameraJet devait marquer son arrivée spectaculaire dans l’hygiène dentaire après six années de développement et 38 brevets déposés. Si aucun blessé ne semble avoir été signalé à ce stade, voir un produit à 479 euros disparaître des rayons dix jours après son lancement ressemble tout de même à un sérieux crash industriel.

articles.title: Pour encadrer l’IA, Donald Trump dévoile un code de bonne conduite
articles.text:
Ce mardi 29 septembre, Donald Trump a réuni au sein de la Maison Blanche les principaux acteurs américains de l’IA. Nous pouvons noter la présence de : Greg Brockman (OpenAI), Elon Musk (X), Jeff Bezos (Amazon), Jensen Huang (Nvidia), Sundar Pichai (Google), Dario Amodei (Anthropic), Satya Nadella (Microsoft), Lisa Su (AMD) ou encore Mark Zuckerberg (Meta).
L’objectif a été de présenter un code de bonne conduite censé encadrer le développement de l’intelligence artificielle. Chaque entreprise est libre d’y adhérer ou non. À l’heure actuelle, six dirigeants de grandes entreprises de l’IA l’ont signé, à savoir : Sundar Pichai (Google), Dario Amodei (Anthropic), Mark Zuckerberg (Meta), Greg Brockman (OpenAI), Elon Musk (X) et Jensen Huang (Nvidia).
Un code de bonne conduite pour encadrer le développement de l’IA
Ce code de bonne conduite, qui tient sur une page, s’articule autour de quatre volets. Premièrement, il en revient à chaque entreprise d’instaurer des contrôles internes « stricts » pour encadrer le développement de l’intelligence artificielle, plus particulièrement dans certains secteurs (cybersécurité, biosécurité, menaces chimiques), et pour « s’assurer que ses modèles ne piratent pas ou n’accèdent pas à des systèmes techniques de manière non intentionnelle ».
Deuxièmement, une équipe interne à l’entreprise doit s’assurer que les contrôles soient bien appliqués et les éventuels problèmes corrigés. Troisièmement, un auditeur ou évaluateur externe indépendant doit s’assurer de la bonne application des contrôles internes de l’entreprise. Enfin, quatrièmement, chaque entreprise doit désigner un comité indépendant du conseil d’administration pour superviser et recevoir les rapports des équipes gérant les contrôles. Notons tout de même que le document indique qu’ « avec le temps, cela aura peut-être du sens de codifier ces pas dans des lois et des régulations ».
Quelle valeur pour ce code de bonne conduite ?
Il avait été récemment rapporté qu’OpenAI, Google et Anthropic travaillaient sur leur propre gendarme de l’IA, faute de régulation du gouvernement américain. Nous pourrions dire que c’est maintenant chose faite avec la signature de Donald Trump sur le document de bonne conduite mentionné ci-dessus. Cependant, quelle est la valeur de ce document qui invite chaque entreprise à établir ses propres normes de régulation ? D’autant plus sous la supervision d’un président américain qui prône un développement de l’IA « avec prudence », mais sans trop de contraintes non plus. Donald Trump l’a encore répété ce 29 septembre : « Nous sommes les leaders, et nous allons conserver notre avance ».
Sans surprise, Jensen Huang (Nvidia) et Mark Zuckerberg (Meta) se sont félicités de ce code de bonne conduite. Seul Dario Amodei (Anthropic) semble avoir montré quelques réserves : « La technologie présente des risques réels. Le mécanisme, la façon dont on affronte ces risques, est encore en discussion. »
De son côté, Donald Trump a estimé que ce code de bonne conduite est « presque comme une constitution, d’une certaine manière ». Quoi qu’il en soit, à un mois des élections de mi-mandat, ce document permet au président américain d’afficher une position prenant en compte les alertes sur les dangers de l’IA, tout en répondant aux demandes de certains patrons de l’IA qui réclament une régulation du secteur.

articles.title: Europa quiere triplicar la capacidad de sus centros de datos. Hay un problema: depende de demasiadas empresas de fuera
articles.text:
Europa se prepara para necesitar mucha más capacidad de cómputo de la que tiene hoy. La expansión de la inteligencia artificial, los servicios cloud y las cargas de trabajo cada vez más exigentes empuja a construir infraestructura a una escala mucho mayor, y Bruselas quiere acelerar ese proceso dentro de la propia Unión. El problema aparece cuando miramos qué hay dentro de esos centros de datos y quién está detrás de las tecnologías que los mantienen funcionando: en varias de las capas más importantes, la UE sigue dependiendo de compañías y cadenas de suministro situadas fuera de sus fronteras.
La escala de ese salto ya está sobre la mesa. La Comisión Europea presentó en junio el Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA), una propuesta con la que pretende al menos triplicar la capacidad de los centros de datos de la UE durante los próximos cinco a siete años y llevarla a un nivel capaz de cubrir las necesidades de empresas y administraciones públicas de aquí a 2035. No hablamos, por tanto, de triplicar el número de instalaciones, sino la capacidad disponible. El plan todavía debe recorrer el proceso legislativo europeo, pero anticipa una expansión que implicaría una enorme demanda de servidores, chips y toda la infraestructura necesaria para operarlos.
Europa quiere crecer sin aumentar su dependencia
Ahí es donde esa ambición choca con una realidad bastante menos favorable. GEA y DECISION calculan que las compañías con sede en la Unión capturan solo el 6% del mercado europeo de semiconductores para centros de datos, el 7% de la fabricación y ensamblaje de servidores y el 8% del valor asociado a infraestructura cloud. Dicho de otra forma, la inmensa mayoría del valor generado por esas capas tecnológicas queda en manos de empresas con sede fuera de la UE. Eso no significa, sin embargo, que todo ese hardware se fabrique fuera de sus fronteras: el informe mide quién captura el valor, no únicamente dónde se produce.
Y la dependencia no está concentrada en un único eslabón. Asia oriental concentra buena parte de la fabricación avanzada de semiconductores, mientras la UE mantiene una fuerte dependencia de empresas estadounidenses en el diseño de chips y el mercado de servidores también está encabezado por fabricantes de fuera de la Unión. Europa conserva, sin embargo, fortalezas extraordinarias: la neerlandesa ASML es actualmente el único fabricante mundial de sistemas de litografía EUV, esenciales para producir los chips más avanzados. El problema está en el conjunto de la cadena y en el ritmo: desde 2021, la demanda europea de sistemas de servidores ha crecido a un ritmo anual del 36%, frente al 20% de la fabricación dentro de la UE.
El siguiente escalón tampoco cambia demasiado la fotografía. La Comisión Europea señala que la cuota de los proveedores de la UE en el mercado cloud cayó del 29% en 2017 al 15% en 2022 y se ha mantenido en torno a ese nivel, mientras tres grandes hiperescaladores no pertenecientes a la Unión concentran más del 70% del mercado europeo. No debemos confundir ese porcentaje con el 8% mencionado antes: GEA mide cuánto valor de la infraestructura cloud capturan compañías con sede en la UE, mientras aquí hablamos de participación de los proveedores de servicios.
UN VISTAZO A...
Hasta aquí hemos hablado de industria y mercado, pero la dependencia se vuelve más delicada cuando afecta a servicios esenciales. La Comisión utilizó como ejemplo el intento de Kyndryl de adquirir Solvinity, proveedor de infraestructura para servicios de la administración neerlandesa utilizados por 16,5 millones de ciudadanos. El Gobierno de Países Bajos terminó bloqueando la operación en mayo de 2026 tras evaluar cuestiones relacionadas con el interés público, la autonomía digital y la protección de infraestructuras críticas.
Ese es el desequilibrio que Bruselas quiere empezar a corregir. La Comisión plantea las propuestas de CADA y Chips Act 2.0 como dos piezas complementarias: una busca facilitar el despliegue de mucha más capacidad de computación y la otra aprovechar esa demanda para reforzar el diseño, la fabricación y la cadena de suministro de semiconductores en la UE. El objetivo no pasa por aislar el mercado europeo, sino por reducir una dependencia que hoy atraviesa varias de sus capas fundamentales.

articles.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Spaces to help humans and agents work together
articles.text:
OpenAI launches ChatGPT Spaces to help humans and agents work together
Spaces is ChatGPT's human-AI collaboration environment
- Spaces is replacing Library for Pro, Business and Enterprise users
- It puts your documents, colleagues, generative AI and agentic AI in one place
- Live Pages are a new document type that AI can automatically keep up-to-date
As AI continues to evolve from much more than just basic generative conversations to greater autonomy, OpenAI has launched a new ChatGPT Spaces interface to serve as the new environment for human-AI collaboration.
Within Spaces, multiple colleagues will be able to collaborate with each other alongside ChatGPT, but it's also a shared space for other OpenAI tools like Codex and the newly-announced, always-on Dots.
The introduction of Spaces largely replaces the now-outgoing Library tab for Pro, Business and Enterprise users across both desktop and mobile, as well as the web, but it also serves a much bigger purpose than Library ever did.
ChatGPT Spaces replaces Library
The company defines Spaces as a "home for the pages and files you create, upload, and share in ChatGPT, including spreadsheets and presentations."
But importantly, the change also sees the introduction of Pages – new documents that combine "text, images, charts and [other] interactive tools." Instead of ChatGPT generating a document and users having to manually edit or prompt changes, Pages are now live places where connections with apps like Slack, emails and calendars keep data current.
In a set of FAQs, the company also noted that each user has their own ChatGPT and, where applicable, Dot, to interact with, so they can call on AI to make changes or keep things up-to-date.
There's also a meeting plugin in the works, currently available in beta for Pro and Business users via the desktop app only. It "creates private, personalized notes and suggests follow-ups" within the shared Space that's accessible by colleagues.

While OpenAI hasn't set out to replace Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, Spaces does mark a major shift in how workers access their documents, putting documents (via plugins), humans and AI all in one place together.

articles.title: Gong adds auto-enrichment and event-driven agents to its revenue intelligence platform - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Gong adds auto-enrichment and event-driven agents to its revenue intelligence platform
Revenue intelligence startup Gong is expanding its platform with third-party account and contact data, deeper artificial intelligence analysis and tools for building agents that automatically execute sales workflows.
The company used its Gong Celebrate conference in Las Vegas today to launch Mission Callisto, a new feature of its Gong Enrich data enrichment platform that brings information from outside data providers into its Revenue Graph analytical and reporting engine. The release also adds deep research to Gong Assistant and expands dashboards beyond forecasting to track performance across sales, marketing and customer success.
Gong, the business name of Gong.io Ltd., said the updates address a common problem facing revenue teams: Customer conversations and sales activity provide useful context, but they don’t necessarily contain the current contact information and account details sellers need to reach prospects. Missing or outdated records can also limit what AI assistants and agents can access.
“Gong Enrich adds data that may not exist in either place,” co-founder and Chief Product Officer Eilon Reshef said, referring to its Revenue Graph and customer relationship management records. “By bringing information from multiple third-party data providers directly into Gong, teams can fill those gaps and give Gong’s AI and agents a more complete picture of every account and contact.”
Customers can connect to supported data providers and set the order in which Gong queries them. If a provider can’t supply the requested information, Gong moves to the next one on the list.
Customers can use existing subscriptions and credits and spend Gong Credits to fill in any gaps. Partners include ZenLeads, Inc., which does business as Apollo , LeadIQ Inc., Lusha Systems Inc., RocketReach LLC and ZoomInfo Technologies Inc.
Sellers can fill missing contact details with a click, while teams can automate enrichment when specified conditions occur. For example, a bounced email can trigger a search for updated information.
Administrators choose data partners, exclude selected geographies and decide whether incoming information fills empty CRM fields or replaces existing values. Gong also identifies the source for most contact details and allows that information to be passed into the CRM.
Those controls have limits. Reshef said Gong relies on providers’ representations about opt-out and suppression requirements, does not independently verify each contact’s opt-out status and does not guarantee every data point’s accuracy. Customers remain responsible for how they use the information, including outreach.
Prebuilt agents
Another change is the addition of automatic triggers to custom agents. Gong distinguishes Agent Builder, which creates workflows specific to a customer’s business, from Agent Studio, where customers configure Gong’s prebuilt agents.
“The biggest change is that those agents can now be event-driven rather than relying on someone to manually trigger them,” Reshef said.
For example, an agent could respond to a change in status of an enterprise deal by analyzing relevant calls against a company’s risk criteria, summarizing its findings and writing next steps to the CRM. Customers can define triggers, conditions and actions through a visual editor or natural-language instructions, then reuse company-specific expertise across agents.
Deep Mode targets strategic questions requiring broader investigation than Gong Assistant’s existing Quick Mode. For example, a revenue leader might ask what is driving enterprise deal risk during a quarter and what the team should change.
The feature can clarify the question’s scope, plan an investigation and examine deals, conversations, accounts and other signals over time. It might identify recurring security concerns in stalled deals and surface supporting conversations.
“Deep Mode is for bigger strategic questions that require broader analysis, synthesis across multiple signals, and a complete, sourced report,” Reshef said.
The dashboard expansion lets teams define metrics once in Gong Data Studio and reuse them across views. Other Assistant updates embed it in deal and account boards and allow users to create Gong Engage Flows through natural-language requests.
Gong Enrich, Deep Mode and the expanded dashboards are generally available. Automatically triggered custom agents and the other Assistant enhancements will roll out later this year.

articles.title: Quelles sont les meilleures offres de PC portables gaming en RTX Série 50 pour la rentrée à la Fnac ?
articles.text:
Quelles sont les meilleures offres de PC portables gaming en RTX Série 50 pour la rentrée à la Fnac ?
Pour la rentrée, la Fnac aligne une belle sélection de PC portables équipés des cartes graphiques GeForce RTX Série 50, de la porte d'entrée abordable à la machine surpuissante. Quatre modèles se détachent, chacun pensé pour un usage précis, du premier PC gaming au poste hybride jeu-création de contenu. On fait un rapide tour d'horizon pour découvrir ces références particulièrement intéressantes.
Au-delà des chiffres bruts, ce qui réunit ces machines, c'est le socle commun des GeForce RTX Série 50. Ces cartes s'appuient sur l'architecture Blackwell et une nouvelle génération de cœurs dédiés à l'IA, qui ouvrent la porte au DLSS 4.5 et 5, la suite de technologies de rendu neuronal de NVIDIA. Concrètement, voici comment fonctionne le DLSS : l'IA vient épauler le GPU pour générer des images supplémentaires et améliorer la netteté, ce qui se traduit par plus de fluidité et de détails sans exiger une puissance de calcul démesurée. Mais toutes les cartes offrent des performances différentes, et c'est justement l'intérêt de cette sélection.
Acer Nitro V 17 AI : la porte d'entrée grand écran
Premier prix de cette sélection, l'Acer Nitro V 17 (disponible à 1039,99€ au lieu de 1439,99€ chez la Fnac) vise ceux qui veulent se lancer dans le jeu sur PC sans se ruiner, avec un grand format d’écran à la clé. L’appareil associe un processeur AMD Ryzen 5, 16 Go de RAM, un SSD de 512 Go et une carte GeForce RTX 5050 8 Go, le tout sur un écran 17,3 pouces Full HD à 144 Hz. Notez que même sur cette carte d'entrée de gamme, le DLSS 4.5 et sa génération multi-images (Multi Frame Generation) permettent de gagner en fluidité sur les jeux récents, ce qui sera assurément un vrai coup de pouce pour tenir un framerate confortable sans sacrifier les détails visuels. Et évidemment, son grand écran en fait un choix pertinent pour qui privilégie le confort visuel à la maison.
Gigabyte A16 : le modèle polyvalent, entre jeu et création à petit prix
Le Gigabyte A16 (que vous pouvez trouver à 1029,99€ au lieu de 1399,99€ chez la Fnac actuellement) monte d'un cran côté processeur avec un AMD Ryzen 7, tout en conservant 16 Go de RAM, un SSD de 512 Go et une GeForce RTX 5050 8 Go. Son écran 16 pouces à 165 Hz apporte un supplément de fluidité appréciable. Et c’est d’ailleurs là que la dimension création prend le relais sur le jeu pur : les cartes RTX ouvrent l'accès à la plateforme NVIDIA Studio, qui accélère nativement de nombreux logiciels créatifs (montage vidéo, 3D ou retouche photo) avec des pilotes optimisés pour la stabilité. Autant dire qu’il s’agit là d’un modèle particulièrement adapté à l'étudiant ou le créateur en herbe qui veut une machine capable de jouer le soir et de travailler ses projets le reste du temps.
Gigabyte Aero X16 : le format créatif qui pousse plus loin
Toujours chez Gigabyte, l'Aero X16 (en réduction de 500€ chez la Fnac, disponible actuellement pour 1299,99€) assume plus nettement encore son positionnement hybride. Il embarque un processeur AMD Ryzen AI 9, 16 Go de RAM, un SSD de 1 To et une GeForce RTX 5060 8 Go, sur un bel écran 16 pouces WQXGA à 165 Hz. Notez que cette définition plus élevée que le Full HD profite autant aux jeux qu'aux travaux créatifs exigeant de la précision. D’ailleurs, au-delà du jeu, de la plateforme Nvidia Studio ou encore du DLSS, notez que les cartes RTX 5060 ouvrent aussi la voie aux usages d'IA en local : génération d'images, assistants et traitements créatifs peuvent tourner directement sur la machine grâce aux cœurs Tensor dédiés, sans dépendre du cloud. C’est donc, dans l’ensemble, une machine taillée pour les créateurs qui veulent aussi pouvoir jouer, tout en demandant un peu plus de performances à leur appareil.
MSI Raider 16 HX : la bête de course de la sélection
Enfin, on aborde la machine reine de la sélection : au sommet, le MSI Raider 16 HX (accessible à 2 299,99€ pour les adhérents Fnac au lieu de 2699,99€) joue dans une toute autre catégorie. Il combine un processeur Intel Core Ultra 7, 32 Go de RAM, un SSD de 1 To et une puissante GeForce RTX 5070 Ti 12 Go, sur un écran 16 pouces QHD à 240 Hz. Il est par ailleurs équipé d’une RTX 5070 ce qui le rend, au même titre que les autres cartes de la gamme RTX Série 50, éligible au tout nouveau DLSS 5. Lancé en septembre 2026 et exclusif à ces dernières, le DLSS 5 ne se contente plus de multiplier les images : il mise sur le rendu neuronal pour injecter en temps réel un supplément de réalisme dans l'éclairage et les matières. Associé à la dalle 240 Hz, l'ensemble vise une expérience de jeu haut de gamme sans compromis. Et autant dire qu’il s’agit du modèle le plus performant de toute la sélection.
Découvrez toute la sélection
Ces quatre machines ne sont qu'un aperçu. Que l'on cherche un premier PC gaming abordable, une configuration hybride pour jouer et créer, ou une bête de course pour le jeu exigeant, il y a une GeForce RTX Série 50 pour chaque profil et chaque budget. Actuellement, vous pouvez retrouver tout un tas d’offres de PC portables en RTX Série 50 chez la Fnac pour la rentrée, afin de mieux comparer l'ensemble des références disponibles.

articles.title: TSMC’s 3-nm Ramp Looks Different in Historical Context - EE Times
articles.text:
TSMC’s 3-nm process is approaching an important milestone. In the second quarter of 2026, it accounted for 30% of wafer revenue, just behind 5 nm at 33%. Recent industry reports suggest that 3 nm could become TSMC’s largest revenue-generating process family during the second half of the year.
But its current size does not tell us how quickly it got there. To compare ramp speed, I used TSMC’s quarterly disclosures to track each node’s share of wafer revenue over its first six quarters as a separate line item, for 10 nm, 7 nm, 5 nm, and 3 nm. Aligning the nodes by age, not calendar date, makes the ramps directly comparable.
In the second reported quarter, 10 nm had already reached 25% of wafer revenue. At the same point, 7 nm was at 23%, 5 nm at 20%, and 3 nm at 15%. By the sixth reported quarter, the picture looked very different. 10 nm had fallen to 6%, 5 nm was at 23%, 3 nm at 26%, and 7 nm had reached 35%.
The newest process generation has not automatically produced the fastest revenue-share ramp. The starting conditions were different.
TSMC’s 7-nm process inherited a large part of the manufacturing platform already developed for 10 nm. The company said more than 95% of the tools were compatible between the two processes and expected that commonality to support a very fast yield ramp. Its commercial ramp benefited from a considerable amount of process learning carried over from the previous generation.
5 nm involved a different transition. TSMC planned extensive use of EUV at 5 nm in part to reduce process complexity, while 7 nm had been developed around much of the established 10 nm tool base.
Revenue-share curves capture more than customer adoption. They also reflect how much manufacturing learning a new process inherits before the first meaningful revenue appears.
The demand behind each node was changing at the same time. 10 nm was strongly associated with performance-driven mobile products, although TSMC also targeted server and graphics applications. By 7 nm, the process was being positioned for both mobile and high-performance computing. 5 nm was optimized from the outset for both mobile and HPC.
The size of the manufacturing operation changed too. TSMC’s annual capacity was just over 12 million 12-inch-equivalent wafers in 2019. By 2024, it was approximately 17 million.
Revenue grew much faster than capacity. When 7 nm reached 35% of wafer revenue in the fourth quarter of 2019, TSMC reported consolidated quarterly revenue of roughly NT$317 billion (~$9.95 billion). When 3 nm reached 26% at the same stage of its ramp in the fourth quarter of 2024, quarterly revenue was roughly NT$868 billion (~$27.2 billion).
Those figures should not be multiplied directly because TSMC reports node mix as a percentage of wafer revenue while the company figure is consolidated revenue. But they show how much the economic base underneath the ramp had changed.
The generations also overlap. In the fourth quarter of 2024, 3 nm represented 26% of wafer revenue, while 5 nm was still 34%, and 7 nm another 14%.
2 nm is now the next test. Everyone will watch how quickly it gains share. But the percentage alone will again reflect several things at once, including how much manufacturing learning carries over from the previous generation, which products move first, and how much economic value TSMC generates from each increment of leading-edge capacity.
3 nm may not be TSMC’s fastest revenue-share ramp, but it may still become one of its largest.

articles.title: Sam Altman compara el impacto de la IA con el “Renacimiento” y no con la revolución industrial
articles.text:
Sam Altman, director ejecutivo de OpenAI, planteó que la inteligencia artificial (IA) debería impulsar un nuevo “Renacimiento” que amplíe la creatividad y las capacidades humanas, en lugar de reproducir un modelo similar al de la Revolución Industrial, en el que las personas terminen convertidas en engranajes de una maquinaria.
El empresario expuso esta visión durante la conferencia anual de desarrolladores DevDay, celebrada este martes en San Francisco, donde reflexionó sobre el papel que debería desempeñar esta tecnología en la sociedad.
PUBLICIDAD
“La gente suele hablar de la IA como una nueva Revolución Industrial. A mí me parece bastante desagradable”, afirmó Altman ante los asistentes. Con estas palabras, cuestionó una perspectiva que relaciona el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial principalmente con la automatización del trabajo y defendió, en cambio, su potencial para ampliar las posibilidades de las personas.
Sam Altman plantea una inteligencia artificial centrada en las capacidades humanas
Durante su intervención en DevDay, Altman propuso una visión de la inteligencia artificial que no se limite a reemplazar tareas que actualmente realizan las personas. En su planteamiento, esta tecnología debería proporcionar herramientas que permitan a los usuarios desarrollar nuevas ideas, explorar su creatividad y ampliar sus capacidades.
PUBLICIDAD
La comparación con el Renacimiento busca representar un periodo de transformación cultural e intelectual en el que el conocimiento, las artes y la creatividad adquirieron un papel central. Al utilizar esta referencia, el ejecutivo de OpenAI planteó un futuro en el que la IA contribuya a que las personas puedan hacer más cosas, en lugar de reducir su participación en diferentes actividades.
Por el contrario, la Revolución Industrial representa un proceso histórico marcado por la mecanización de la producción y la transformación del trabajo. Aunque también generó avances económicos y tecnológicos, su referencia permite a Altman expresar sus reservas frente a un futuro en el que la inteligencia artificial se valore únicamente por su capacidad para sustituir el esfuerzo humano.
PUBLICIDAD
Su planteamiento se produce en medio de un debate cada vez más amplio sobre el impacto de la IA en el empleo, la educación y las actividades creativas. La expansión de los modelos generativos ha permitido automatizar tareas de redacción, programación, diseño y análisis de información, lo que ha abierto nuevas oportunidades, pero también ha generado interrogantes sobre el papel que tendrán las personas en estos ámbitos.
Las declaraciones llegan en medio de los desafíos de seguridad de OpenAI
La visión de Altman sobre el futuro de la inteligencia artificial coincide con un periodo de mayor atención sobre la seguridad de los modelos desarrollados por OpenAI. La compañía canceló el lanzamiento previsto de GPT-6.1 Astra después de determinar que el sistema no cumplía con sus estándares de seguridad.
PUBLICIDAD
La decisión puso de relieve los desafíos que afrontan las empresas tecnológicas a medida que desarrollan modelos con capacidades más avanzadas. Antes de poner una herramienta de este tipo a disposición del público, las compañías deben evaluar los riesgos asociados con su funcionamiento y determinar si cumple con los requisitos establecidos para su despliegue.
El caso de Astra también se relaciona con un incidente de seguridad protagonizado por modelos de prueba de OpenAI. Según la información difundida por la compañía, estos sistemas explotaron una vulnerabilidad y consiguieron acceder sin autorización a determinados sistemas de la plataforma Hugging Face.
Este episodio expuso uno de los riesgos asociados con el desarrollo de agentes de inteligencia artificial capaces de interactuar con servicios externos. A medida que estos sistemas adquieren más autonomía para ejecutar instrucciones y utilizar herramientas digitales, también aumenta la importancia de establecer límites que eviten accesos indebidos y otras acciones no autorizadas.
PUBLICIDAD
El futuro de la IA también depende de cómo se utilice
Las declaraciones de Altman reflejan una discusión que va más allá de las capacidades técnicas de los modelos. El impacto de la inteligencia artificial también dependerá de las decisiones que tomen las empresas que la desarrollan y de la manera en que sus herramientas se incorporen a las actividades cotidianas.
La propuesta de impulsar un nuevo Renacimiento plantea que la IA puede funcionar como un instrumento para potenciar el trabajo humano. Sin embargo, esa perspectiva convive con los desafíos que supone automatizar tareas, proteger la información y garantizar que los sistemas se comporten de manera segura.
En ese contexto, las palabras del director ejecutivo de OpenAI sitúan la creatividad y las capacidades humanas en el centro de su visión sobre el futuro de esta tecnología. Al mismo tiempo, la cancelación de Astra y el incidente relacionado con Hugging Face muestran que el desarrollo de modelos más avanzados también exige resolver problemas de seguridad antes de ampliar su disponibilidad.

articles.title: AOC Announces AGON PRO AGP257FT Monitor with 1000 Hz (1050 Hz OC) Fast IPS Panel
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 30th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
AOC Announces AGON PRO AGP257FT Monitor with 1000 Hz (1050 Hz OC) Fast IPS Panel
AGON by AOC, the world's leading gaming monitor brand, announces the AGON PRO AGP257FT, the fastest monitor in its line-up to date. The 24.5-inch (62.2 cm) Full HD esports monitor runs at a native 1000 Hz refresh rate, which can be overclocked to 1050 Hz, and pairs this with 0.3 ms GtG (minimum), VESA DisplayHDR 400 and hardware-based eye comfort features. The AGP257FT is designed for professional esports players and gamers in competitive fast-paced titles and is expected to be available from Q1 2027.
At the core of the AGP257FT is an oxide-based Fast IPS panel. Fast-response liquid crystal materials and an advanced panel architecture drive pixels faster than conventional LCD designs, overcoming the voltage-response limits that typically hold LCD panels back at extreme refresh rates. The result is smoother motion, lower frame delay and more immediate visual feedback during flick shots, quick turns and rapidly changing scenes. At 1000 Hz, the AGP257FT draws a new frame every millisecond.
VESA DisplayHDR 400 and 20-zone local dimming add brightness and depth in compatible titles. The panel covers 99% of the sRGB and 90% of the DCI-P3 colour space at a typical brightness of 450 nits, and every unit ships with a colour and brightness uniformity report.
Eye comfort for long sessions
Training blocks and tournament days mean hours in front of the screen. The AGP257FT handles eye comfort at hardware level:
The fully adjustable stand offers 150 mm of height adjustment along with tilt, swivel and pivot, with built-in measurement markings that make it easy to maintain or replicate the preferred position, while a quick-release mechanism makes it easy to take the monitor to LAN events and tournaments. The included QuickSwitch keypad gives fast access to game modes and settings.
Pricing and availability
The AGON PRO AGP257FT is expected to be available from Q1 2027. Local pricing in European regions will be announced closer to launch.

articles.title: TP-Link opens global preorders for its first Wi-Fi 8 router, but ban keeps it out of US market — US left off launch list as FCC freeze refuses to thaw
articles.text:
TP-Link opens global preorders for its first Wi-Fi 8 router, but ban keeps it out of US market — US left off launch list as FCC freeze refuses to thaw
The Archer 8 Ultra is launching across Europe and Australia, but the U.S. has given TP-Link the cold shoulder
Today is a big day for TP-Link, as the company revealed that it has opened preorders for its first Wi-Fi 8 hardware. The previously announced Archer 8 Ultra router makes the company’s first entry into what will become a fully stocked portfolio covering Wi-Fi 8 standalone and mesh routers, access points, and client adapters. Interestingly, TP-Link makes it clear that preorders kicked off today in the United Kingdom, Germany, Australia, and other global markets. 
Given that the United States is a key consumer market for TP-Link, the fact that the country is left off the preorder list is telling, but not exactly a surprise to anyone who has been following the wireless industry over the past six months. TP-Link has sat on the sidelines as competitors including Netgear, Asus, and Amazon gained Conditional Approvals from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to sell their hardware in the U.S. Without the Conditional Approval, companies are effectively banned from selling new wireless hardware in the country that wasn't already approved by the FCC.
So, while earlier Wi-Fi 7 gear from TP-Link that received FCC certification can still be sold, any new Wi-Fi 7 or Wi-Fi 8 products are effectively blocked from the market. The company has made several critical moves to position itself as a U.S. company, including incorporating TP-Link Systems in California, but those moves have been challenged in legal filings.
At this point, there haven’t been any clear signs that the U.S. government will lift its freeze on TP-Link hardware, so until that time comes, the Archer 8 Ultra will remain unavailable stateside. And it’s a shame, because the Archer 8 Ultra, which utilizes a Broadcom Wi-Fi 8 chipset, will deliver up to 33 percent more real-world throughput compared to TP-Link’s Wi-Fi 7 hardware, and 24 percent more consistent throughput when operating in high-interference conditions.
The Archer 8 Ultra will feature two auto-sensing 10 Gbps WAN/LAN ports and four 2.5 Gbps LAN ports. TP-Link says that the router covers up to 3,600 square feet and will support up to 200 devices.
"Wi-Fi 8 sets a new foundation, and we’ve built beyond it,” said Jim Poder, Senior Vice President of R&D at TP-Link. “Archer 8 Ultra combines our Wi-Fi 8 StabilityEngine with intelligent antenna technology and AI-powered optimization to deliver what matters most: a smarter, more reliable network that’s easier to use.”
TP-Link’s Wi-Fi 8 family will expand in Q1 2027 with a Deco 8 Ultra mesh router, and a Roam 8 travel router in Q2 2027. Throughout the year, further additions will come in the form of new PCIe/USB wireless adapters, access points, and range extenders.

articles.title: Rakuten France ferme ce soir, voici comment récupérer vos factures et vos points avant qu'il ne soit trop tard
articles.text:
La plateforme Rakuten France ferme ce mercredi 30 septembre à 23h59, faute de repreneur. Si vous y avez déjà acheté un produit, deux échéances à retenir : les points Club R expirent ce soir, et l’accès à votre compte, avec l’historique de vos commandes, sera définitivement fermé le 10 novembre. Voici comment ne rien perdre.
Une fermeture actée après l’échec de plusieurs reprises
À partir de jeudi 1er octobre, il ne sera plus possible d’acheter ni de vendre sur la plateforme, ex-PriceMinister, lancée en 2000 et rachetée par le groupe japonais Rakuten en 2010. Environ 180 salariés sont concernés. La fermeture touche aussi l’Espagne, qui dépend de la même structure.
Rakuten France cherchait un repreneur depuis plusieurs mois. Selon la direction, citée par Le Monde, aucune offre ne remplissait les trois critères fixés : préservation des emplois, conditions financières et pérennité de l’activité à long terme. Le comité économique et social a rendu un avis négatif sur ces propositions. Pixmania, l’un des candidats évincés, avait dénoncé en juillet le rejet de son offre, qu’il disait « financièrement soutenue » par ses actionnaires, et craint que sa candidature n’ait servi qu’à remplir l’obligation légale de rechercher un repreneur avant une fermeture (loi Florange).
En cause, un déclin engagé depuis une dizaine d’années : le nombre de clients a chuté de 33 % en dix ans, et le trafic de 42 % sur la même période, sous l’effet notamment du succès des plateformes chinoises comme Shein et Temu.
Vendeurs : vos fonds restent en sécurité
Si vous vendiez sur Rakuten, votre argent n’est pas géré directement par la plateforme mais par Mangopay, son partenaire de paiement agréé. « Vos fonds restent en sécurité et la continuité des paiements liés à vos ventes demeure une priorité absolue », assure Rakuten sur sa page dédiée aux vendeurs. Les sommes qui n’auraient pas encore été reversées au 10 novembre resteront disponibles : après cette date, il faudra simplement s’adresser directement à Mangopay pour les récupérer. Rakuten conseille de finaliser sans tarder toute vérification d’identité en attente, pour faciliter le versement.
Récupérez vos factures avant le 10 novembre
Rakuten n’édite pas de facture lui-même : c’est le vendeur qui la fournit. Si vous avez acheté à un professionnel et que vous n’avez pas votre facture, demandez-la depuis le suivi de commande, dans votre compte. Sans réponse, une réclamation ouverte au même endroit permet de relancer le vendeur. Pour un achat effectué auprès d’un particulier, Rakuten fournit à la place une attestation d’achat, qui fait office de reçu : rendez-vous dans « Tous mes achats », puis « Imprimer l’attestation d’achat », uniquement depuis le site, l’application mobile ne proposant pas cette option.
Dans tous les cas, mieux vaut agir avant le 10 novembre, 23h59, car c’est la date à laquelle l’accès à votre compte et à tout votre historique de transactions sera définitivement fermé. Pensez aussi à conserver de votre côté les e-mails de confirmation, des captures d’écran des annonces, ainsi que les coordonnées et le nom officiel des vendeurs : dans deux ans, un simple pseudonyme ne suffira plus.
Trois dates à retenir
- Ce mercredi 30 septembre, 23h59 : dernier moment pour acheter, vendre ou utiliser vos points Club R
- 10 novembre, 23h59 : fermeture définitive de l’accès aux comptes et à l’historique de commandes
- 30 novembre : dernier jour pour joindre le service client au sujet des transactions en cours, paiements et reversements
Vos points Club R expirent ce soir
Vous avez encore des points Club R ? Rakuten indique que vous pouvez les utiliser normalement jusqu’à la fermeture de la plateforme, ce mercredi 23h59, mais ils seront ensuite « définitivement perdus ». Trois options avant l’échéance : les dépenser sur le site, les échanger contre des cartes cadeaux, ou demander leur virement sur votre compte bancaire.
Vos garanties restent valables, mais le recours change
La fermeture de la plateforme n’annule pas vos garanties. La Garantie Rakuten couvre les litiges pendant 14 jours après la livraison, ou 30 jours après la confirmation de commande si le colis n’avait pas de numéro de suivi, y compris si ce délai se termine après la fermeture. Le service client reste joignable par téléphone, chat ou formulaire.
Passé ce délai, c’est la garantie légale de conformité qui prend le relais, pour deux ans après la livraison d’un produit neuf. Le vendeur professionnel en reste seul responsable, que Rakuten existe encore ou non. Si Rakuten promet de le relancer « dans la mesure du possible » en cas de silence du vendeur, le traitement de la demande dépendra ensuite entièrement de lui, d’où l’intérêt de conserver une preuve d’achat.
Rakuten précise enfin que les données personnelles restent traitées dans le cadre du RGPD, avec un engagement à prévenir les clients en cas d’évolution.

articles.title: Meta targets SMBs with Muse AI that can run your business for you
articles.text:
Meta targets SMBs with Muse AI that can run your business for you - but will anyone actually need it?
Meta launches Muse for Small Business
- Meta adds new SMB plan for Muse always-on agents
- It works with Instagram/Facebook and third-party connections
- Most Muse use cases should be free, but there are paid plans for more tokens
Meta has expanded its agentic AI platform with the launch of Muse for Small Business.
In a similar vein to OpenAI's new Dots service, Muse users can give their agents a goal or objective and let the agent carry out work independently, palming off some of the more administrative workloads like running parts of the business or finding new customers.
Meta argues that small businesses are a key target for Muse because they wouldn't typically have dedicated resources across marketing, finance and other admin, hence the agentic boost.
Muse for Small Business
Importantly, Muse is likely to be highly tailored toward Meta's own products, hence the company's examples spanning connections with "Instagram professional account analytics, Facebook Pages, and Meta ad accounts."
Crucially, Muse also works with other existing connectors, like Asana, Dropbox, Shopify, Slack and Zoom, making it much more than a Meta-only tool.
Just like its high-profile rival, Muse also continues to work in the background toward pre-defined objectives, surfacing relevant information or issues that require human intervention. Some use case examples include scanning emails and calendars for the most important actions, and drafting new ad campaigns based on current trends.
Meta argues that Muse is set to be free "for most of what people need," but two additional paid plans are also available for businesses who want to go all-in on agentic AI, including the $20/month Power plan (500M weekly tokens) and the $100/month Max plan (3B weekly tokens).

Interestingly, Meta's approach took a consumer product and reframed it for businesses. Muse launched earlier this month for US and Canadian customers before getting an SMB variant, but OpenAI's Dots landed with business users in mind, and there's currently no word on whether a consumer variant could launch.
