articles.title: Das 9-to-5-Diktat: Warum starre Arbeitszeiten für Abendtypen zum Gesundheitsrisiko werden
articles.text:
Neue Studie zeigt: Nachteulen verlassen den Beruf deutlich früher
Menschen mit einer späten inneren Uhr haben ein um rund 70 Prozent höheres Risiko, vorzeitig aus dem Erwerbsleben auszuscheiden. Zu diesem Ergebnis kommt ein Team von Forscher:innen der finnischen Universität Oulu, wie in einer im Fachjournal Occupational and Environmental Medicine veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist.
Die Mediziner:innen analysierten die Daten von 5.679 Teilnehmer:innen einer finnischen Geburtskohorte aus dem Jahr 1966. Die Beobachtung erstreckte sich über einen Zeitraum von zwölf Jahren, in dem das Lebensalter der Personen von 46 auf 57 Jahre anstieg.
Dabei zeigte sich, dass sogenannte Nachteulen deutlich häufiger eine Erwerbsminderungsrente in Anspruch nehmen mussten als Morgentypen (Lerchen) oder keine den beiden Extremen zuzuordnende Personen. Dieser Unterschied blieb bei beiden Geschlechtern als konstante statistische Größe bestehen, selbst als externe Faktoren wie Bildungsebene, Einkommen und der spezifische Beruf herausgerechnet wurden.
Methodik zur Bestimmung der Chronotypen
Die Zuordnung zu den jeweiligen Biorhythmen erfolgte nicht allein auf Basis subjektiver Einschätzungen der Proband:innen. Das Team der Universität Oulu nutzte validierte Fragebögen, die detailliert erfassten, wie schwer das Aufwachen fiel und wie stark die Müdigkeit in der ersten halben Stunde des Tages ausgeprägt war.
Zusätzlich glichen die Wissenschaftler:innen diese Selbsteinschätzungen mit genetischen Daten aus einer früheren Erhebung ab. Dieser polygene Score für frühes Aufstehen bestätigte die biologische Basis der Angaben, wodurch eine Verfälschung der Ergebnisse durch rein persönliche Vorlieben unwahrscheinlich wurde.
Etwa 10 Prozent der befragten Männer und 12 Prozent der Frauen fielen am Ende der Auswertung in die Kategorie der Nachteulen. Die Gruppen der Morgen- und Zwischentypen machten jeweils mehr als 40 Prozent der Gesamtmenge aus.
Gesundheitliche Ursachen bei Abendtypen
Die Auswertung ergab, dass fast die Hälfte der männlichen und gut 43 Prozent der weiblichen Nachteulen ihre allgemeine Gesundheit als schlecht einstuften. Sie berichteten häufiger über Schlaflosigkeit, geringere körperliche Aktivität und einen ausgeprägten sozialen Jetlag.
Dieser Jetlag entsteht, wenn die biologisch präferierte Schlafzeit klar von den tatsächlichen Zeiten an Arbeitstagen abweicht. Laut der ergänzenden Zusammenfassung auf StudyFinds führt diese Diskrepanz langfristig zu chronischem Schlafmangel, der kognitive Fähigkeiten beeinträchtigt und den körperlichen Abbau beschleunigt.
Erst als die Forscher:innen eben jene gesundheitlichen Einschränkungen und die absolvierten Arbeitszeiten in ihre Modelle einbezogen, schrumpfte die statistische Lücke zwischen Eulen und Lerchen messbar. Vor allem die geleisteten Wochenstunden und das Arbeiten in Schichten hatten einen starken Einfluss auf die Wahrscheinlichkeit eines frühen Berufsausstiegs.
Konsequenzen aus starren Schichtmodellen
Während über 70 Prozent der Nachteulen angaben, in regulären Tagesjobs zu arbeiten, war der Anteil an Nachtschichten bei ihnen dennoch signifikant höher als bei den Lerchen. Die Forscher:innen betonen, dass ein typischer Arbeitstag in Finnland um acht Uhr morgens beginnt, was einer Zeit entspricht, in der späte Chronotypen noch unterhalb ihres maximalen Leistungsniveaus operieren.
Die Daten offenbarten zudem weitere soziodemografische Auffälligkeiten innerhalb der untersuchten Gruppen. Nachteulen waren zwar im Durchschnitt höher gebildet, lebten aber seltener in einer Ehe oder festen Partnerschaft und waren häufiger von Erwerbslosigkeit betroffen.
Eine Erwerbsminderungsrente wird in dem untersuchten finnischen System nur bewilligt, wenn ein medizinisches Gutachten eine dauerhafte und schwerwiegende Einschränkung der Arbeitsfähigkeit bestätigt. Das bedeutet, dass der beobachtete Ausstieg nicht auf eine fehlende Motivation zurückzuführen ist, sondern auf nachweisbare medizinische Diagnosen fußt.
Die Studienautor:innen weisen explizit darauf hin, dass dieser Verlust von erfahrenen Arbeitskräften ein ernst zu nehmendes Problem für die Volkswirtschaften darstellt. Der unfreiwillige Abschied aus dem Berufsleben geschieht während der produktivsten Kernjahre einer normalen Karriere.
Trotz der umfassenden Datenlage weisen die Forscher:innen auf gewisse Limitierungen ihrer Methodik hin. So basierte die Erfassung des Chronotyps lediglich auf einer einmaligen Befragung im Alter von 46 Jahren, weshalb sich die Resultate vornehmlich auf diese spezifische Altersgruppe beziehen.
Das unbedingte Festhalten an konventionellen Arbeitszeiten, die sich vorwiegend am Rhythmus von Lerchen orientieren, benachteiligt die Gruppe der Eulen demzufolge systematisch. Ob asynchrone Arbeitsmodelle diese Entwicklung stoppen können, müssen weitere Analysen klären, da die Studie lediglich Beobachtungen festhält, aber keine Kausalität zwischen flexiblen Arbeitszeiten und einer sinkenden Rentenquote isolieren konnte.

articles.title: This gaming laptop from Asus has to be the most spectacular I’ve ever tested — but you’ll have to pay a small fortune for it
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
We’ve seen dual-screen laptops before, but they’re still something of a rarity, especially in a full-fledged gaming laptop. So it’s impressive what Asus has managed to achieve here, packing two 3K OLED displays (with touchscreen functionality no less), a detachable keyboard, and an RTX 50 series GPU into a form factor that isn’t as cumbersome as you might imagine. It also performs exceptionally well, although battery life is underwhelming at best. It’s a niche prospect for sure, but if you must have two displays in a laptop and don’t want to sacrifice graphical power, the ROG Zephyrus Duo is unmatched.
Reasons to buy
- +Fantastic dual display setup
- +Still relatively compact
- +Top-tier performance
Reasons to avoid
- -Not the most premium of constructions
- -Fans prone to making noise
- -Poor battery life
Why you can trust TechRadar
Asus ROG Zephyrus Duo (2026): Two-minute review
The ROG Zephyrus Duo is a mighty gaming laptop with an outstanding spec, which includes not one but two 3K OLED touchscreens.
It looks, though, bely its capabilities. There isn’t much branding or brashness here, and the dark colorway keeps things modest. It also lacks the sleekness of some models, with its various jutting edges and angles sullying its contours. The materials don’t seem all that premium, either. However, the ROG Zephyrus Duo is still a solidly made machine, and considering what lurks beneath, it’s surprisingly thin and compact.
The way the dual displays are set up is clever and well engineered, too. The keyboard can be detached to reveal the second screen, and there’s a sturdy stand underneath the unit to prop up both displays. These solutions provide plenty of scope for your preferred setup, and the various hinges operate smoothly while providing plenty of stability.
What’s more, there’s a generous selection of ports on the ROG Zephyrus Duo, matching some of the best gaming laptops on this front. In addition to two Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports and two USB-A ports, you also get an SD card reader and an HDMI output.
My review unit was the top-spec model with the RTX 5090 GPU, so naturally its gaming performance was superb. It ran Cyberpunk 2077 between 50-60fps on the highest preset and at full resolution. There was a lot of fan noise and heat, but the former isn’t too disruptive, and the latter is confined to the underside of the unit.
Both displays are as vivid and as sharp as you would expect given their OLED technology and 3K resolution. Their touchscreens are responsive and sufficiently smooth, although they can feel a little grabby at times. They’d be better served by a stylus, but unfortunately you’ll have to provide your own, since the ROG Zephyrus Duo doesn’t come with one.
The keyboard functions well, whether attached to the bottom screen or detached and connected via Bluetooth. The keys have a generous travel and a tactile feel, which makes them great for typing. However, they feel a little cramped when gaming in the WASD position, and it’s a shame the layout isn’t full size, given the space available. The integrated touchpad works well for cursor navigation, thanks to its large surface.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
As with most gaming laptops, the battery life of the ROG Zephyrus Duo is a weak point. It didn’t even last four hours when I ran a movie on a continuous loop, a poor result even by the measly standards of your typical gaming laptop.
The ROG Zephyrus Duo certainly demands a large chunk of money, but it's an undeniably high-end device with just about the best performance you could wish for in a portable gaming machine. What’s more, there aren’t many dual-screen laptops built for gaming at this level, so the ROG Zephyrus Duo is a must if that’s a priority for you.
Asus ROG Zephyrus Duo (2026) review: Price & availability
- Starts from $4,499.99 / £3,999.99 / AU$8,999
- Available now
- Incredibly expensive
Given its almighty spec, it shouldn't come as a surprise that the ROG Zephyrus Duo has a price tag to match. Exact model specifications vary with region, but the starting price is $4,499.99 / £3,999.99 / AU$8,999. For this, you get an RTX 5070 Ti GPU, 32GB of RAM, and 1TB of storage.
If a dual-screen setup is a must for your laptop, you could also look at the Lenovo Yoga Book 9i. It too comes with Bluetooth keyboard, but also comes with a mouse and a stylus, both of which the ROG Zephyrus Duo omits. Additionally, it costs a lot less than ROG Zephyrus Duo, although the big drawback is that it doesn’t have a dedicated GPU, so it isn’t one for heavy gamers.
If you don’t need dual screens, but just want an all-conquering gaming laptop, then the Razer Blade 18 is about the best we’ve tried in this category. We were overawed by its performance, while we also loved its keyboard, display, and form factor. It too has a seriously daunting price, though.

Asus ROG Zephyrus Duo (2026) review: Design
- Understated looks
- Smart and versatile dual-screen setup
- Generous port selection
The ROG Zephyrus Duo cuts a rather unassuming figure, with its dark gray colorway and lack of branding. On the lid, the diagonal strip that’s become the mark of the Zephyrus line doesn’t add much interest. But the matte finish on the lid is a nice touch.
However, the rest of the unit’s materials don’t look or feel particularly premium. Its form is quite utilitarian, too, lacking the totally flat and flush surfaces of more sleek laptops. Thankfully, though, it feels very solid, and although the top display enclosure is quite thin and has some flex to it, it’s sturdy enough.
The ROG Zephyrus Duo is actually quite a discreet device. There’s no denying its thickness, but when you consider it hides a second screen and a detachable wireless keyboard, as well as featuring up to an RTX 5090 GPU, it’s quite impressive Asus has managed to make it this compact. It’s still expectedly heavy, though.
Two 3K OLED touchscreen displays are the standout feature of the ROG Zephyrus Duo. You can set them up in various ways: by reclining the main display back past 180 degrees so you can prop the unit like a tent, or leave the laptop in the standard position and simply remove the keyboard to use the display underneath. This would be perfect for drawing or handwriting while you keep your eyes on the main display. It’s a shame, though, that the ROG Zephyrus Duo doesn’t come with a stylus despite supporting them, although if you’re an enthusiastic creative you may already have one you can use.
The hinge offers a smooth pivot and provides plenty of stability, no matter what angle you have the main display at. However, it doesn’t allow for a full 360-degree rotation, so the ROG Zephyrus Duo can’t be used like a tablet — although this wouldn’t exactly be practical, given its size and weight.
Perhaps the best way to make use of the ROG Zephyrus Duo’s dual displays is to unfold the integrated kickstand underneath the unit so that both displays are stacked on top of each other. This stand provides a reassuring stability and, despite how thin it is, it doesn’t feel flimsy.
Switching between dual- and single-screen use is made easy thanks to the removable keyboard. It’s magnetically attached to the bottom screen, so it simply requires a light pry to detach it. At the same time, it’s also very stable when in place; I didn’t experience any wobbling or displacement when using it.
When detached, it connects to the ROG Zephyrus Duo via Bluetooth, which you enable by flicking a switch on the side of the keyboard. It charges when attached to the bottom screen, but you can also charge it using the USB-C port on its side when it’s not.
Its build quality is less impressive than the rest of the ROG Zephyrus Duo, though. The soft outer material feels cheap and is prone to scuff marks and the like, while the board itself is quite flimsy. However, this is a price worth paying for its lightness, and it remains stable while typing.
Given its real estate, the layout is disappointingly compromised. It seems like there’s space to include a number pad or at least more navigation keys. The arrow keys are inconveniently small, too, although the integrated touchpad is a good size at least.
I was also glad to see a number of ports on board the ROG Zephyrus Duo. In addition to two Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports and two USB-A ports, there’s also a full-sized SD card reader, an HDMI port, and a 3.5mm headset jack. These ports are spread quite evenly across both sides of the unit and are sensibly positioned.
Asus ROG Zephyrus Duo (2026) review: Performance
- Phenomenal performance
- Consistent fan noise
- Keyboard not great for gaming

Battery Life (TechRadar movie test): 3 hours and 37 minutes
My review unit was equipped with the top-tier RTX 5090, which, combined with the Intel Core Ultra 9 and 64GB of RAM, made for blistering performance. I was getting around 30fps on Cyberpunk 2077 with the maximum Ray Tracing: Overdrive preset and the maximum 2880 x 1800 resolution selected, with DLSS set to Balanced. This jumped to between 50-60fps when I enabled Frame Generation on top.
As expected, though, fan noise accompanied this performance. Thankfully, it’s not too disruptive, but more troubling is the fact that the fans can whir up sporadically, even when fairly lightweight tasks are being undertaken, such as browsing the web.
Scorching temperature can also afflict the ROG Zephyrus Duo, although mercifully the heat is confined to the underside of the base, with the commonly contactable surfaces, such as the keyboard and bottom screen, remaining perfectly comfortable to touch. Using the kickstand also helps to dissipate some of the heat.
As you would expect, the two 3K OLED displays are a visual treat, with plenty of sharpness, contrast, and vividness. They both have small bezels, which helps them to maximize their respective 16-inch canvases, and they do a reasonable job of keeping reflections at bay thanks to their high brightness levels.
Their touchscreen functionality is also quite good. Although they can be a little grabby at times, they’re smooth enough for the most part. They’re also quick to respond to inputs.
The keyboard is a tactile affair, with low-profile keys that offer more dampening and travel than you might expect, but they're still snappy, making for a fast and satisfying experience. They’re comfortably spaced for typing, although I found gaming in the WASD position a little cramped and awkward. The large touchpad makes general navigation practical, though.
Asus ROG Zephyrus Duo (2026) review: Battery life
- Short-lived, even by gaming laptop standards
- Quick to charge
For such a large and feature-packed gaming laptop, it’s no real surprise that the ROG Zephyrus Duo isn’t a particularly enduring machine. However, it drains faster than many other gaming laptops. It lasted just over three and a half hours in our movie playback test, and this was with just the main screen active.
To put this result into context, the Lenovo Legion 7i Gen 10, another 16-inch gaming laptop, lasted almost eight hours in the same test, while the Razer Blade 18, which is 18-inches, lasted closer to eight and a half hours.
Fortunately, the ROG Zephyrus Duo is quick to charge, taking between 60-90 minutes to fully replenish, which is more impressive.
Should I buy the Asus ROG Zephyrus Duo (2026)?
Scorecard
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
| Value | The ROG Zephyrus Duo is incredibly expensive, but that’s hardly a surprise considering its two displays and superlative spec. | 3 / 5 | 
| Design | That dual-display setup is well thought-out, but while the construction is strong, it doesn’t look or feel especially premium. | 4 / 5 | 
| Performance | My review unit had just about the highest spec a gaming laptop could have, so naturally outright performance was peerless. The fans frequently make themselves known, though, and the keyboard isn’t the best for gaming. | 5 / 5 | 
| Battery life | Disappointing, even by gaming laptop standards. It’s at least quick to charge, though. | 3 / 5 | 
| Overall Rating | The ROG Zephyrus Duo is a unique proposition in the gaming laptop market, and it's certainly an accomplished machine. The poor battery and awkward keyboard are drawbacks, but the real issue is the price. Still, if you need an incredibly powerful dual-screen laptop, nothing fits the bill better. | 4 / 5 | 
Buy it if…
You want two displays
I don’t think I’ve seen a more powerful laptop with dual displays, and their clever versatility is an added bonus.
You want a high spec
With heaps of RAM and storage space, not to mention a top-tier CPU and GPU, there aren’t many portable devices more powerful.
Don't buy it if…
You’re on a budget
With that godlike spec comes an unholy price tag.
You want a long battery life
Not many gaming laptops can keep going all day, but the ROG Zephyrus Duo is particularly short lived.
Asus ROG Zephyrus Duo (2026) review: Also consider
Razer Blade 18
The Razer Blade 18 is easily one of the best gaming laptops we’ve ever tested. It gets pretty much everything right: the performance is phenomenal, the keyboard is a dream to use, and even the form factor is reasonable for an 18-inch machine. More remarkable is that it has a superior battery life to many of its rivals. Read our full Razer Blade 18 review.
Lenovo Yoga Book 9i 
If you want a powerful dual-screen laptop, but don’t need all that gaming prowess, the Yoga Book 9i is a fine choice. We loved this laptop’s everyday performance and interesting arrangements for its two displays. Its port selection is a little disappointing, but it’s a veritable bargain next to the ROG Zephyrus Duo. Read our full Lenovo Yoga Book 9i review.
How I tested the Asus ROG Zephyrus Duo (2026)
- Tested for a few days
- Used for a variety of tasks
- Plenty of gaming laptop experience
I tested the ROG Zephyrus Duo for several days, during which time I used it for a variety of tasks besides gaming, such as general browsing and video streaming.
I also ran our comprehensive series of benchmark tests, designed to assess every facet of a gaming laptop. I tested the battery life by running a movie on a continuous loop.
I’ve been PC gaming for over a decade, and have used a variety of systems and components during that time. I’ve also reviewed many gaming laptops previous to the ROG Zephyrus Duo, including other Asus models.
- First reviewed: August 2026

Lewis Maddison is a Reviews Writer for TechRadar. He previously worked as a Staff Writer for our business section, TechRadar Pro, where he gained experience with productivity-enhancing hardware, ranging from keyboards to standing desks. His area of expertise lies in computer peripherals and audio hardware, having spent over a decade exploring the murky depths of both PC building and music production. He also revels in picking up on the finest details and niggles that ultimately make a big difference to the user experience.

articles.title: Android dit non à l'Union européenne : Google refuse d'ouvrir l'OS à ChatGPT et Claude
articles.text:
Depuis le 16 juillet, deux décisions de la Commission européenne imposent à Google d’ouvrir Android aux assistants IA concurrents et de partager ses données de recherche, au titre du DMA, le règlement européen sur les marchés numériques. Ce mardi 29 septembre, l’entreprise a annoncé contester les deux textes devant le Tribunal de l’Union européenne, à Luxembourg. Le recours décidera de votre liberté de remplacer Gemini par l’assistant de votre choix.
ChatGPT au bouton, Claude à la voix : l’Android que Bruxelles exige
La décision Android, adoptée après six mois d’instruction, contraint Google à ouvrir onze fonctions du système aux assistants concurrents. Un appui long sur le bouton d’accueil pourra réveiller un autre service que Gemini, et chaque éditeur pourra définir son propre mot d’activation, l’équivalent du « Hey Google » maison. Les assistants tiers obtiendront aussi l’accès au contexte de vos applications, à l’automatisation d’actions à l’écran, aux modèles embarqués comme Gemini Nano et à l’exécution en arrière-plan. L’essentiel doit arriver avec Android 18, au plus tard le 1er août 2027 ; l’écoute simultanée de plusieurs mots d’activation attendra Android 19, à l’été 2028. Les accès les plus sensibles passeront par un programme de certification, dont les conditions définitives sont attendues pour le 1er mai 2027.
Google refuse d’ouvrir ces portes et met la sécurité en avant. Confier à des applications tierces un micro toujours actif, la lecture de l’écran et des automatisations système reviendrait, d’après ses équipes, à « saper le modèle de sécurité fondamental d’Android ». La firme brandit aussi le risque d’injection de commandes : des instructions cachées dans une page ou un document, qui détournent un agent IA sans que son propriétaire ne s’aperçoive de rien.
Vos recherches, l’autre trésor que Google ne veut pas céder
La seconde décision touche à plus intime encore : vos requêtes. À partir de janvier 2027, Google devra fournir aux moteurs concurrents, chatbots IA compris, ses données de recherche anonymisées (requêtes, clics, classements), à prix encadré, dès lors que le demandeur dépasse 50 000 utilisateurs européens par mois. L’entreprise plaide que ces données racontent nos vies, « des préoccupations de santé à l’intimité », et qu’un partage mal protégé causerait un « préjudice irréparable » à la vie privée des utilisateurs.
Bruxelles oppose ses garde-fous : anonymisation des données, consentement explicite de l’utilisateur pour les accès sensibles, conservation limitée à treize mois et audits indépendants imposés aux bénéficiaires. Le 23 juillet, la Commission a déjà infligé 890 millions d’euros d’amende à Google pour deux manquements distincts au même règlement. Ignorer les décisions de juillet exposerait cette fois l’entreprise à des sanctions pouvant atteindre 10 % de son chiffre d’affaires mondial.
En attendant les juges, rien ne bouge sur votre écran : Gemini reste seul à décrocher quand vous pressez le bouton, et le calendrier fixé par Bruxelles n’a pas varié à ce stade. Si la Commission tient bon, votre Android devra faire de la place aux assistants rivaux d’ici à l’été 2027. Si Google l’emporte, l’assistant de votre fidèle téléphone restera ce qu’il est aujourd’hui : préinstallé, exclusif et non négociable.
 👉🏻 Suivez l’actualité tech en temps réel : ajoutez 01net à vos sources sur Google, et abonnez-vous à notre canal WhatsApp.
Source : Reuters

articles.title: 5 Lessons from The Psychology of Money about wealth
articles.text:
5 Lessons from The Psychology of Money about wealth
Discover five powerful lessons from The Psychology of Money by Morgan Housel about building wealth, making smarter decisions, and thinking long term.
When people think about wealth, they often focus on investment strategies, stock market predictions, or complex financial formulas.
Yet, according to Morgan Housel's bestselling book The Psychology of Money, financial success is often less about knowledge and more about behaviour. Through engaging stories and timeless insights,
Housel explores how emotions, habits, and personal experiences shape the way people think about money. The book argues that wealth is not simply a result of earning more; it's often the result of making better decisions consistently over time.
Here are five valuable lessons from The Psychology of Money about building and preserving wealth.
1. Wealth is what you don't see
Many people associate wealth with expensive cars, luxury homes, or designer products. Housel challenges this idea by explaining that true wealth is often invisible. Real wealth consists of assets that have not yet been spent. It is the money saved, invested, and allowed to grow over time.
People who appear wealthy may not necessarily be financially secure, while those living modestly may be building substantial wealth behind the scenes.
The lesson is simple: focus less on looking rich and more on becoming financially secure.
2. Saving matters more than income
A high salary does not automatically lead to wealth. What matters is how much of that income is saved and invested. Housel emphasises that building wealth often depends on creating a gap between what you earn and what you spend. Even people with average incomes can accumulate significant wealth if they consistently save over long periods.
This lesson highlights the importance of financial discipline rather than relying solely on earning more money.
3. Time is the most powerful wealth-building tool
One of the book's central themes is the power of compounding. Small amounts of money invested consistently can grow dramatically when given enough time. Housel points to the success of long-term investors who benefited not only from good decisions but also from allowing those decisions to compound over decades.
The lesson encourages patience. Wealth is often built gradually rather than through quick wins or sudden breakthroughs.
4. Financial freedom is the ultimate luxury
Many people chase money to buy things, but Housel argues that the greatest benefit of wealth is control over your time.
Financial freedom provides the ability to make choices without being entirely dependent on a paycheck or external pressures. It allows people to spend time on meaningful work, relationships, hobbies, and personal goals.
According to the book, having the freedom to decide how you spend your days is one of the most valuable forms of wealth.
5. Avoid comparing your finances to others
Comparison can be one of the biggest obstacles to building wealth. It often encourages unnecessary spending and pushes people to pursue lifestyles they cannot comfortably afford. Housel explains that there will always be someone with more money, a larger house, or a more impressive lifestyle. Constant comparison creates a cycle where satisfaction becomes difficult to achieve.
Instead, the book encourages readers to define their own financial goals and make decisions based on their personal values rather than external expectations.
Final thoughts
The Psychology of Money offers a refreshing perspective on wealth. Rather than focusing on complicated financial strategies, it highlights the behaviours and mindsets that often determine long-term success.
The book reminds readers that wealth is not about impressing others or chasing endless growth. It is about making thoughtful decisions, saving consistently, thinking long term, and creating the freedom to live life on your own terms.
For anyone interested in building a healthier relationship with money, these lessons provide a valuable foundation that extends far beyond finance.

articles.title: Scott Jenson critique Liquid Glass et les pubs de Windows, deux symptômes d'un bureau délaissé
articles.text:
Scott Jenson a créé le groupe Interface chez Apple dans les années 1980 avant de diriger l'expérience mobile de Google pendant cinq ans. Dans une conférence publiée par la communauté KDE, il estime qu'Apple comme Microsoft ont arrêté d'améliorer l'ergonomie de leur système pour les utilisateurs. Liquid Glass vise à unifier un écosystème rapprochant macOS de l'iPhone, tandis que Windows cumule les décisions contestées.
macOS : Liquid Glass au service de l'écosystème, pas du bureau
Chez Apple, Jenson s'en prend à Liquid Glass, cette refonte visuelle qui joue sur la transparence avec des effets de verre dépoli. Pour l'expert, l'interface ne répond à aucun besoin propre de l'ordinateur de bureau. Visuellement et fonctionnellement, elle sert à rapprocher le Mac de l'iPhone. L'homme critique aussi les nouvelles fonctions destinées à solidifier les liens entre les appareils Apple. Selon lui, elles ne font que renforcer le fameux jardin clos d'Apple. Chaque fonction qui lie les appareils entre eux rend le départ vers la concurrence plus difficile.
Chez Apple, Jenson a travaillé sur les Human Interface Guidelines, autrement dit, le référentiel qui régit la cohérence des interfaces de la marque, sur Mac System 7, une version historique du système, puis sur le Newton, la tablette avant l'heure.
Si Jenson estime que la cohérence entre les plateformes peut être utile, il avance qu'Apple privilégie la cohésion de son écosystème plutôt au détriment de l'ergonomie et sans prendre en compte les usages du bureau.
Windows : OneDrive, Recall et publicités
Jenson est encore plus sévère avec les choix de Microsoft. Il cite l'usage imposé de OneDrive, le service de stockage en ligne de l'éditeur ; le lancement raté de Recall, la fonction de Windows qui enregistre l'activité de l'utilisateur pour la rendre consultable ; et les "publicités partout". Selon lui, ces trois problèmes différents ont tous les mêmes points communs : le cloud, l'intelligence artificielle et les revenus publicitaires. Et tous passent avant l'expérience utilisateur.
Durant sa conférence, Jenson partage une anecdote personnelle : il a passé un entretien chez Microsoft vers 2018 pour prendre la tête de l'expérience utilisateur de Windows. C'était en plein cycle de Windows 10. Lui défendait déjà l'idée que le bureau devait évoluer, mais sans changer les habitudes de centaines de millions d'utilisateurs et avec un arbitrage entre continuité et progrès. De son côté, Microsoft expérimentait déjà des interfaces inspirées du mobile, lesquelles sont arrivées plus tard dans Windows 11 en 2021.

articles.title: iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop review: Strong gaming value and extras
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The iBuyPower Slate is a well-executed mid-range gaming desktop that pairs attractive styling, thoughtful extras, and strong RTX 5070-powered gaming performance. While its Ryzen 7 7700X3D isn't as capable in productivity workloads as Intel-based competitors, gamers looking for a capable 1080p and 1440p machine with quality included peripherals will find plenty to like.
Reasons to buy
- +Strong gaming performance
- +Attractive tempered glass case with RGB lighting
- +Quality included mechanical keyboard and mouse
- +360 mm liquid cooler with integrated status display
Reasons to avoid
- -Productivity performance trails similarly-priced Intel systems
- -Cooling fans can get loud under CPU-heavy workloads
- -RGB software lacks per-component control
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
The $1,999 iBuyPower Slate arrives with a formula that's hard to argue with: an RTX 5070, a Ryzen 7 7700X3D, a 360mm liquid cooler, and a tempered-glass chassis with plenty of RGB lighting. It even goes beyond expectations by including gaming peripherals that don't feel like afterthoughts.
But in an increasingly competitive mid-range desktop market, attractive extras and gaming prowess alone aren't always enough. The question is whether the Slate's gaming-first focus justifies its price when rivals offer stronger all-around performance for similar money.
Design of the iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop
There’s no mistaking the Slate for anything but a gaming machine. It’s designed to be seen inside and out, with a full-view tempered glass side panel. The front panel’s triangle glass partially shows off a trio of 120 mm RGB fans. The tower sits firmly in mid-tower territory, at 8.7 x 19.3 x 19.5 inches.
The mesh covering the rest of the front and top permits airflow and should do a decent job of blocking dust, though the case’s only removable air filter is under the bottom-mounted power supply.
Inside, the Slate’s blacked-out interior offers an RGB light strip running along the power supply compartment and up the front panel. Additional lighting comes from the two memory DIMMs. The GPU, an Asus Dual RTX 5070 in our review unit, lacks illumination. The lighting can be controlled via the Hyte Nexus app, though not on a per-component basis. (See the Software section later in this review.)
iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop Specifications
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 7 7700X3D | 
| Motherboard | ASRock B560M-CX R2.0 | 
| Memory | 32GB DDR5-5200 (2x 16GB) | 
| Graphics | Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 (Asus Dual Gaming OC; 12GB GDDR7, 2,542 MHz boost clock) | 
| Storage | 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD (Patriot P410) | 
| Networking | RZ616 Wi-Fi 6E | 
| Front Ports | USB-C 3.2, 2x USB-A 3.2, headphone and microphone jacks | 
| Rear Ports | USB-C 3.2 (10 Gbps), USB-A 3.2 (10 Gbps), 2x USB-A 3.2 (5 Gbps), 4x USB 2.0, Ethernet, HDMI, audio jacks | 
| Power Supply | 750 watts, non-modular | 
| Cooling | 360 mm liquid (iBuyPower) | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 Home | 
| Dimensions (WxDxH) | 8.7 x 19.3 x 19.5 inches (221 x 490 x 495 mm) | 
| Price (as configured) | $1,999.99 | 
Ports and Upgradeability on the iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop
Mid-tower desktops tend to include lots of ports, and iBuyPower’s Slate doesn’t disappoint. The top-mounted front connectivity includes one USB-C and two USB-A (all 5 Gbps) plus separate headphone and microphone jacks. The positioning of these ports works best if the desktop is placed on the floor; it’s less ideal on a desk.
Rear connectivity on the ASRock B650M-CX motherboard includes one USB-C 3.2 (10 Gbps), one USB-A 3.2 (10 Gbps), two USB-A 3.2 (5 Gbps), four USB 2.0, Ethernet, HDMI, and audio jacks. Though there are no truly high-speed ports, they aren’t expected outside of high-end towers with pricier motherboards. The desktop also includes Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth – the antennas must be connected as shown here for meaningful range.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The side panels come off with a tug at the top rear, hinging outward and away. Seven 120 mm fans – three front, three on the top-mounted 360 mm CPU cooling radiator, and one rear – provide plentiful airflow. Cabling is reasonably tidy, though the bundle of unused cables from the non-modular 750-watt power supply is a bit of a mess.
The CPU cooler is more than a basic model, with an LED screen showing CPU temperature, frequency, and load. The display can’t be customized, though it can be toggled off in the Hyte Nexus app.
The Slate’s expansion options include one open PCIe x16 slot and four DIMM slots, two of which are unpopulated. The motherboard offers two M.2 2280 drive slots. There are two 2.5-inch drive sleds behind the motherboard, but no room for a 3.5-inch drive.
Gaming and Graphics on the iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop
We are testing the iBuyPower Slate with a Ryzen 7 7700X3D processor, GeForce RTX 5070 GPU, and 32GB of RAM.
Playing 007 First Light, at 3840 x 2160 with High settings and DLSS enabled, I observed between 60 and 70 frames per second (FPS) in outdoor scenes and closer to 80 FPS indoors. Using DLSS was required for smooth gameplay, as I saw roughly half the FPS without it.
Our comparison desktops include the Asus ROG G700 (Core Ultra 7 265KF, RTX 5070, $2,029.99 when reviewed) and the CyberPowerPC Gaming Desktop GXi3800BSTV2 (Core Ultra 7 270K Plus, RTX 5070, $2,309.99), both mid-tower systems with the same GPU but Intel processors.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
At 1080p, iBuyPower’s Slate proved competitive overall, matching the Asus and CyberPowerPC in Shadow of the Tomb Raider (Highest settings), Cyberpunk 2077 (Ray Tracing Ultra), and Black Myth: Wukong (Cinematic). However, its Ryzen 7 7700X3D paid dividends in Far Cry 6 (Ultra), where its 185 FPS was well ahead of the Asus (110 FPS) and CyberPowerPC (141 FPS). It led by a similar amount in Red Dead Redemption 2, with 145 FPS against the Asus’ 120 FPS and the CyberPowerPC’s 126 FPS.
The Slate generally didn’t differentiate itself from the other desktops at the 4K resolution, an expected result since that resolution is almost always GPU-limited and these systems all rely on an RTX 5070. The exception was Far Cry 6, where the Slate’s 97 FPS greatly outperformed the 80 and 81 FPS produced by the Asus and CyberPowerPC, respectively.
Overall, despite its Ryzen 7 7700X3D not being nearly as powerful for general use as the Core Ultra 7 265K and Core Ultra 7 270K Plus featured in our competing systems, it can outperform both chips in games.
We stress-test gaming desktops running 15 loops of the Metro: Exodus benchmark at RTX settings. The iBuyPower desktop posted highly stable performance, averaging 145.7 FPS across all runs with less than a one frame variance across all runs. The Ryzen 7 7700X3D’s average temperature was 43 degrees Celsius and its average clock was 4.29 GHz. The RTX 5070 ran at 64 C and had an average core clock of 2.64 GHz.
I noticed a decent amount of fan noise from the Slate particularly when the CPU was stressed, causing the triple-fan CPU cooler to quickly ramp up to high speed. The fan noise was hardly noticeable for daily use and was relatively low while gaming as well.
Productivity Performance on the iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop
We tested the iBuyPower Slate gaming desktop featuring a Ryzen 7 7700X3D processor, 32GB of dual-channel DDR5-5200 RAM, and a 1TB PCIe 4.0 solid-state drive (a Patriot P410 as tested).
Productivity performance isn’t a strong point for this Slate configuration. Though its Ryzen 7 7700X3D remains potent for gaming, its previous generation eight-core architecture is outmuscled by the Core Ultra 7 K-class chips in both the Asus and CyberPowerPC systems, particularly the latter with its refreshed Core Ultra 7 270K Plus. The delta was significant: iBuyPower's system scored 14,222 in Geekbench multi-core versus 22,485 for CyberPowerPC, and took 3:35 to complete our 4K to 1080p Handbrake transcoding test versus just 2:03 for the Asus and 1:45 for the CyberPowerPC. The iBuyPower system does, however, include a decent storage drive, proving competitive in our 25GB file transfer test.
Despite the Slate’s performance delta versus the Core Ultra 7 systems, this PC is still highly capable for daily productivity and moderate content creation, such as video editing. Only those squeezing every last drop of performance out of their CPU will find it compelling to go with a more powerful chip than the Ryzen 7 7700X3D.
Keyboard and Mouse with the iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop
The Slate includes much better than average peripherals. The mechanical keyboard is the standout. Though not stated in the specs, it feels like it uses linear switches favored by gamers for their predictability. It felt rock solid in my testing and wasn’t overly loud. The keyboard supports RGB backlighting, though not per-key – the lighting can be set in the included Hyte Nexus app for various colors and patterns. You can also control the lighting through keyboard shortcuts – Fn+Ctrl cycles colors, Fn+Left/Right arrows alter brightness, Fn+Space Bar disables lighting, and Fn+Alt cycles through 16 backlighting patterns, such as breathing, pulsing, and steady. It’s also nice to see that the keyboard uses a detachable USB-C cable.
The mouse is also better than average, though it’s only for right handers. The standard buttons offer a solid feel, with two side buttons and a notched scroll wheel. The DPI button behind the scroll wheel switches between 1,200, 2,400, 3,500, 5,500, and 7,200 DPI, which are visually indicated by the DPI button illuminating in red, blue, green, purple, and yellow, respectively. The mouse fits my medium-size hand well. It’s internally backlit in RGB color, which can be configured in Hyte Nexus or toggled through 10 modes pressing the button on the underside. Patterns include color streaming, steady, and breathing, to name a few.
Software and Warranty on the iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop
Besides the usual preinstalled Windows 11 apps, iBuyPower only preloads one app – Hyte Nexus. It provides basic component temperature and frequency monitoring, but its real focus is RGB lighting control.
The menu is confusing – there are tiles for different components, such as the case, but these have no effect since the particular case used in the Slate isn’t recognized. Instead, all the action happens in the Lighting section. Many preset lighting recipes are included, such as Rainbow, Aurora, Ice, Fireplace, and Forest, which even apply to the keyboard and mouse. There are also options for screen mirroring, audio visualization, and static colors. You can save your settings in profiles.
That said, there’s no way to control lighting on a per-component basis – colors and patterns apply to all components at once since they are all connected to ARGB header 1. Confusingly, the app lets you change settings for the other headers, but this has no effect since nothing is connected to them. If the app indicated that those headers aren’t connected, this would have been more straightforward. The Slate nonetheless allows a decent amount of lighting customization despite lacking an advanced lighting controller, which would have increased the cost.
iBuyPower covers the Slate with a one-year parts and labor warranty.
iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop Configurations
We tested the iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop with a Ryzen 7 7700X3D processor, GeForce RTX 5070 graphics card, 32GB (2x 16GB) of DDR5-5200 RAM, and a 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD. A mechanical backlit gaming keyboard and mouse are included in the box.
Best Buy offers several other variations of the Slate. A $1,679.99 starter model included a Core i7-14700F and RTX 5060 while a $1,799.99 model stepped up to a Core Ultra 7 265F and RTX 5060 Ti. Above our test model, a $2,299.99 variant included a Ryzen 9 9900X3D, while a range-topping $2,999.99 model offered a Ryzen 9 7900X, an RTX 5080, and a 2TB SSD.
Bottom Line
iBuyPower’s Slate gets the mid-tier gaming desktop formula almost exactly right. Visually, its RGB lighting is attractive and reasonably configurable even if it lacks per-component control, and its RTX 5070 and Ryzen 7 7700X3D comfortably power through today’s games at 1080p and 1440p, with 4K possible using dialed-down visual quality or DLSS. iBuyPower goes above expectations by including a liquid CPU cooler with a built-in screen and by including a mechanical RGB keyboard and gaming mouse.
Where the Slate stumbles, as least in our reviewed configuration, is processing power. Though the Ryzen 7 7700X3D remains potent for gaming, it’s outclassed by Core Ultra 7 K-class chips for general use, which can be had in systems costing similar money. But for pure gamers, this Slate is a standup performer.
Charles Jefferies is a freelance reviewer for Tom’s Hardware US. He covers laptop and desktop PCs, especially gaming models.

articles.title: Gefahr für Marsmissionen: Warum der Darm in der Schwerelosigkeit streikt
articles.text:
Verstopfung auf der ISS: Studie klärt die Ursache für Verdauungsprobleme im All
Auf der Internationalen Raumstation klagen Raumfahrer:innen seit vielen Jahren über eine stark verlangsamte Verdauung und die damit einhergehende Verstopfung. Obwohl die Menüpläne der Besatzung streng kontrolliert werden und die tägliche Nahrungsaufnahme exakt protokolliert wird, ließ sich das Problem bisher nicht durch einfache Anpassungen der Mahlzeiten lösen. Bislang fehlte der Wissenschaft schlichtweg eine fundierte metabolische Erklärung für dieses weitverbreitete Phänomen unter den Bedingungen der Mikroschwerkraft.
Ein Forschungsteam der dänischen Universität Kopenhagen hat in Zusammenarbeit mit der US-Raumfahrtbehörde Nasa nun den biologischen Mechanismus hinter den Beschwerden entschlüsselt. Wie in einer im Fachmagazin Nature Communications veröffentlichten Studie nachzulesen ist, analysierten die Wissenschaftler:innen die Blutproben von 52 weiblichen und männlichen Besatzungsmitgliedern der ISS. Die Proben stammten von Raumfahrer:innen, die zwischen 2006 und 2018 zwei- bis neunmonatige Missionen im Orbit absolvierten, und wurden vor, während sowie nach den Flügen entnommen.
Veränderte Darmtransitzeit auf der ISS
Die Auswertung der Daten offenbarte, dass die fehlende Schwerkraft im Erdorbit die Peristaltik des menschlichen Verdauungstraktes messbar verlangsamt. Das bedeutet, dass die koordinierten Muskelkontraktionen, die normalerweise den Speisebrei durch den Magen-Darm-Trakt schieben, stark an Intensität verlieren. Als direkte Konsequenz verbleibt die aufgenommene Nahrung wesentlich länger im Darm, als es unter den irdischen Bedingungen mit normaler Gravitation der Fall wäre.
Durch diese unnatürlich verlängerte Darmtransitzeit gerät das Gleichgewicht der Darmbakterien aus dem Takt. Die dort ansässigen Mikroorganismen verbrauchen die verfügbaren Kohlenhydrate und Ballaststoffe in kurzer Zeit vollständig, während der Nahrungsbrei noch im Verdauungstrakt festsitzt. Um weiterhin Energie zu gewinnen und das eigene Überleben zu sichern, stellen die Bakterien ihren Stoffwechsel daraufhin zwangsläufig auf alternative Nahrungsquellen um.
Die Mikroorganismen beginnen im nächsten Schritt, die noch vorhandenen Proteine und Aminosäuren zu zersetzen, was in der Biologie als Proteinfermentation bezeichnet wird. Bei diesem bakteriellen Zersetzungsprozess entstehen spezifische Metaboliten, die über die Darmwand direkt in den Blutkreislauf der Astronaut:innen gelangen. Zu diesen Stoffwechselprodukten gehören unter anderem p-Kresolsulfat und Phenylacetylglutamin, deren Konzentration im Körper bei normaler Verdauung auf einem weitaus niedrigeren Niveau verbleibt.
Die dänischen Forscher:innen um Giorgia La Barbera und Henrik M. Roager konnten in den Blutproben der ISS-Besatzung erhöhte Konzentrationen genau dieser Moleküle nachweisen. Diese Stoffwechselprodukte gelten in der Medizin als eindeutige Marker für den Abbau von Proteinen durch das Darmmikrobiom. Die Messwerte zeigten zudem, dass die Proteinfermentation bereits wenige Wochen nach dem Eintreffen auf der Raumstation anstieg und erst nach der Rückkehr zur Erde wieder auf Normalwerte absank.
Metaboliten belasten die Darm-Hirn-Achse
Der stetige Anstieg dieser spezifischen Metaboliten bringt handfeste gesundheitliche Risiken für die Raumfahrer:innen mit sich, die nicht ignoriert werden dürfen. In der Nephrologie werden Verbindungen wie p-Kresolsulfat unter anderem mit fortschreitenden Nierenschäden in Zusammenhang gebracht. Da der Körper diese Stoffe über die Nieren ausscheiden muss, bedeutet eine konstant hohe Konzentration eine andauernde Belastung für das Organ, was auf längeren Missionen zu schwerwiegenden Komplikationen führen kann.
Zusätzlich entfalten diese Stoffe über die sogenannte Darm-Hirn-Achse auch neurologische Auswirkungen, da das Verdauungssystem und das zentrale Nervensystem in einem ständigen biochemischen Austausch stehen. Laut den Aussagen des beteiligten Professors Lars Ove Dragsted gegenüber ScienceDaily reichen die dokumentierten Folgen von einer reduzierten Konzentrationsfähigkeit bis zu einer Beeinträchtigung der psychischen Verfassung. Eine durch diese Metaboliten ausgelöste kognitive Schwäche stellt bei der Bedienung komplexer Raumschiffsysteme eine offensichtliche Gefahr dar.
Solche Einschränkungen stellen insbesondere für zukünftige Langzeitmissionen, die weit über den niedrigen Erdorbit hinausgehen, ein bisher wenig beachtetes Risiko dar. Während Astronom:innen mithilfe von Hochleistungsteleskopen bereits Exoplaneten wie Beta Pictoris d detailliert erforschen, müssen parallel die grundlegenden medizinischen Hürden für bemannte interplanetare Flüge in unserem eigenen Sonnensystem gelöst werden. Eine Reise zum Mars würde mehrere Monate in Anspruch nehmen, in denen die Crew der Mikroschwerkraft ununterbrochen ausgesetzt wäre.
Lösungsansätze für zukünftige Marsmissionen
Raumfahrtagenturen sind folglich gefordert, spezifische Gegenmaßnahmen zu entwickeln, um die gesundheitsschädliche Proteinfermentation bei monatelangen Aufenthalten im tiefen All zu unterbinden. Diskutiert werden primär diätetische Anpassungen, wie die gezielte Verabreichung von Präbiotika und eine drastische Erhöhung des Ballaststoffanteils in der Astronautennahrung. Durch eine solche Umstellung stünde den Darmbakterien über einen wesentlich längeren Zeitraum das bevorzugte Futter zur Verfügung, wodurch der Wechsel zur Proteinfermentation hinausgezögert würde.
Alternativ könnten medizinische Therapien eingesetzt werden, welche die Peristaltik künstlich anregen und auf diese Weise die Darmtransitzeit künstlich verkürzen. Von den Erkenntnissen aus der Mikrogravitation könnten laut den Studienautor:innen schlussendlich auch bettlägerige Patient:innen auf der Erde profitieren. Bei Personen, die zur strikten Bettruhe gezwungen sind, löst die ausbleibende körperliche Bewegung verwandte Veränderungen der Verdauungsabläufe aus, weshalb die nun identifizierten Marker zukünftig bei der Diagnose und Behandlung im Klinikalltag helfen könnten.

articles.title: Una solución para evitar líos de cables en tu mesa: se trata de un dock 17 en 1 para tu portátil en el que puedes montar hasta un SSD
articles.text:
Llevo más de un año con un MacBook Air y, aunque estoy encantado con él, tiene un defecto: muy pocas opciones de conectividad. Esto no es algo que solo esté presente en los portátiles de Apple, sino que también es algo que podemos ver en los equipos de otros fabricantes. Si quiero utilizar el ratón y el teclado que tengo para trabajar (ambos periféricos se conectan con un USB-A), tengo que recurrir a un accesorio que compré en Amazon. Pero, ¿y si necesitas conectar varios monitores? ¿O tener más almacenamiento?
En ese caso, es necesario invertir en algo más completo. Una opción interesante es el nuevo UGREEN Revodok: viene a ser un dock 17 en 1 que está disponible por 380 euros si usamos el código de descuento que aparece en la página web de este fabricante, solo disponible hasta el 11 de octubre. Tras esa fecha, nos podremos seguir beneficiando de un descuento del 5 % si usamos el código 'XATAKA5'.
UGREEN Revodok Maxidok 17-in-1 Thunderbolt™ 5 Docking Station – 8TB, Dual 6K/8K Display for Mac & Windows
Un dock en el que montar hasta 8 TB de almacenamiento
Con un ordenador portátil puedes trabajar en cualquier lado sin necesidad de tener ni un enchufe a mano (mientras te dure la batería). Pero, en casa, puede que necesites tener un espacio de trabajo más completo para conectar uno o varios monitores, periféricos o tarjetas microSD, por ejemplo. Un dock como este de UGREEN es perfecto para ello, pero con el plus de facilitarte mucho la gestión de cables para no tener un lío de ellos en la mesa o el suelo.
¿Qué conexiones ofrece? Lo primero es un puerto Thunderbolt 5 para que conectemos el portátil, el cual se encuentra en la parte trasera y nos permitirá cargarlo de forma simultánea, puesto que tiene una potencia de carga para ese puerto de 140 W. Además, en la parte frontal, tiene tres puertos USB-C (dos de ellos comparten 60 W de potencia de carga), lectores tanto para tarjetas microSD como SD y un jack de 3,5 mm para auriculares. Es importante señalar que la potencia máxima del dock es de 240 W.
También en la parte trasera encontraremos otros dos puertos más Thunderbolt 5 para conectar periféricos o incluso un monitor, un DisplayPort 2.1, un puerto Ethernet 2.5 GbE, tres USB-A y dos puertos dedicados para altavoces y un micro. Todo sin olvidarnos de que, además, en la propia base hay una ranura M.2 NVMe para que podamos conectar un SSD de hasta 8 TB.
De esta forma, tenemos una solución muy versátil para nuestro lugar de trabajo que nos permitirá, desde un único dock, conectar varias cosas a nuestro portátil mientras también podemos estar cargando nuestro móvil a la vez. El principal aliciente de este son los puertos Thunderbolt 5, aunque para aprovecharlos al máximo es necesario que tu equipo también lo sea. Si no lo es, no te preocupes: lo podrás utilizar igualmente, aunque no a su máxima velocidad de transferencia.

articles.title: España necesita nuevas casas pero hay un cuello de botella insalvable: el hormigón y demás materiales cuestan un dineral
articles.text:
Nuestro país necesita más vivienda. El Banco de España calcula que el ritmo de creación de hogares supera hasta tal punto al de la construcción de edificios que acumulamos un déficit de 750.000 casas desde 2021, un agujero que, advierte el organismo, podría ampliarse a un millón de viviendas en los próximos dos años. El problema es que, pese a ese desfase y la gravedad de la crisis residencial, algo que ha quedado patente con el 'decreto Maricarmen', la construcción sigue sin meter sexta. Y no solo por la burocracia o la escasez de suelo edificable.
Hay otro problema que la lastra: los costes.
Pinchazo en las obras. A pesar de la escasez de vivienda que arrastramos, del desequilibrio entre oferta y demanda y del encarecimiento del metro cuadrado, la construcción española no pasa por su mejor momento. Al menos si hablamos de actividad. El último índice de producción del sector (IPCO) publicado por el INE refleja una bajada interanual del 9,8% en julio, un descenso sensible, aunque mejora el retroceso anotado el mes anterior, cuando se cayó más de un 12%.
No son buenos datos porque el IPCO nos dice básicamente si se construye más o menos que hace un año. Y lo que nos revelan los últimos indicadores es que el sector acumula siete meses seguidos a la baja, sin visos de remontada.
El dato: -40,9%. Esos porcentajes nos hablan de una pérdida de fuelle en la construcción en general, lo que incluye también las obras en carreteras, puertos o ferrocarriles, entre un largo etcétera de ingeniería pública y civil. Sin embargo, el IPCO deja un dato revelador: ese pinchazo del 9,8% se explica sobre todo por la fuerte caída en la construcción de edificios, que retrocedió un 35,2% con respecto al verano pasado. Si se corrige el efecto estacional, el desplome es del 40,9%.
¿Qué significa eso? Que no es solo que se construya menos que en 2025, es que ese bajón se nota sobre todo en las obras de inmuebles, las mismas que deberían ayudarnos a inyectar nueva vivienda en el mercado inmobiliario, equilibrar la oferta y la demanda y (en último término) corregir la subida de precios.
"Más difícil y más caro". No es un panorama halagüeño. Sobre todo si tenemos en cuenta que el BE ya ha advertido que el déficit residencial seguirá agravándose y amenaza con alcanzar la barrera del millón de viviendas en 2028. "La actividad constructora en edificios marca un bajón que no ayuda a corregir el desequilibrio entre demanda y oferta de vivienda, con implicaciones en el precio", advierte la OCU, que conecta la caída de producción con una realidad bien conocida en el sector: "Construir vivienda se ha vuelto más difícil y más caro".
¿Tanto se ha encarecido? Sí. Más allá de las trabas burocráticas para construir o la escasez (y bloqueo) de suelo urbanizable en las ciudades, el sector se ha encontrado con un problema que afecta directamente a su rentabilidad: las viviendas quizás estén encareciéndose en el mercado inmobiliario, pero los costes de construcción también lo hacen. Y a un ritmo bastante considerable.
En julio la Asociación Nacional de Constructores Independientes (ANCI) divulgó un informe que concluye que durante los cinco primeros meses de 2026 el precio de los materiales bituminosos y la energía se disparó un 47%. La subida se añade a la registrada en los últimos años por la pandemia y la guerra de Ucrania.
Lo más preocupante es que la situación no parece haber mejorado en los últimos meses, lo que ya ha llevado a ANCI a pedir medidas excepcionales que tengan en cuenta el aumento de gastos que soportan las constructoras. La petición se dirige sobre todo a las obras públicas que se adjudican con un presupuesto pactado.
"Máxima preocupación". ANCI no es la única que ha advertido sobre la deriva de los costes de construcción. A finales de junio la Confederación Nacional de la Construcción (CNC) trasladó al Gobierno su "máxima preocupación" por "la escalada de los costes de producción" y dejaba dos cifras sobre la mesa: la crisis energética derivada de la guerra de Oriente Medio ha afectado a cerca del 90% las constructoras y el 56% reconoce abiertamente haber ralentizado su actividad.
Más o menos por las mismas fechas la Asociación Nacional Española de Fabricantes de Hormigón Preparado (Anefhop) advertía también del "escenario crítico" al que se enfrontaba por la escalada del precio del petróleo, que se suma a "la presión salarial, escasez de transporte e incremento generalizado de costes". Si bien el Brent corrigió su subida hace unos meses, ha vuelto a encarecerse.
En general todas las ramas del sector apuntan al mismo cóctel de factores: la guerra de Irán, costes salariales y la subida acumulada en los últimos años.
¿Tanto han subido? El índice de costes del sector de la construcción, publicado por el Gobierno, muestra una escalada sostenida en los últimos meses que se traslada tanto a las obras de edificación no residencial como las orientadas a creación de vivienda. Un alza que se añade al registrado en 2025, cuando ACR anotó una subida del 5,5% en los costes directos de construcción de edificios.
Para comprender la deriva de los precios viene bien consultar los gráficos del Instituto Valenciano de Edificación, que reflejan un encarecimiento en diferentes materiales, como los bituminosos, con un alza anual del 14,3%, aluminio (23,5%), áridos y rocas (5,1%), plásticos (4,2%), cemento (7,8%) o siderúrgicos (8,4%). Si se amplía el foco a los últimos años, las subidas son aún más pronunciadas.

Os Galaxy Buds 3 FE estão saindo por R$ 485 no Pix com cupom SITE60 no Mercado Livre. Os fones de ouvido wireless da Samsung, que trazem ANC, bateria de longa duração e funções do Galaxy AI, atingem o menor preço já visto pelo Achados, com desconto de 56% sobre o original de R$ 1.099.
Mas seja rápido: o cupom está em modo de “contagem regressiva” e deve esgotar em breve.

Os recursos de Inteligência Artificial da suíte Galaxy AI incluem o Modo Intérprete, que traduz conversas em tempo real; o usuário escuta a voz da outra pessoa em seu idioma, e o celular Galaxy pareado (recurso exclusivo) exibe as respostas traduzidas, sendo uma ótima função em viagens ao exterior.

articles.title: Sony Will Skip CES 2027 After Honda EV Venture Ends
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 30th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Sony Will Skip CES 2027 After Honda EV Venture Ends
Sony has confirmed it will not exhibit at CES 2027 in Las Vegas, ending a run that goes back to the very first show in 1967. A company spokesperson told Bloomberg that neither Sony nor any of its affiliates plan to exhibit at the January event. Sony did not have its own booth at CES 2026 either, but its Sony Honda Mobility joint venture still showed off an Afeela EV prototype at that show. That EV project was apparently the last big reason for Sony to keep showing up. Sony Honda Mobility canceled the Afeela 1 and a planned SUV in March, after Honda reassessed its electrification strategy, and the two companies said they would review the future of the joint venture.
Sony has also been pulling back from consumer hardware elsewhere, with TCL taking a 51% stake in a new joint venture that will assume its home entertainment business, including Bravia TVs. Sony's own statement says it "continuously and strategically" evaluates how it approaches events, and that its focus keeps shifting toward entertainment, intellectual property, and technology that supports creators. For gamers, it looks like PlayStation won't be using a CES stage next year either, although that was somewhat predictable. CES had slowly stopped being a Sony show already, but a 60-year streak ending is still strange to see.

articles.title: Startup Ascerta collects $18M in funding to help enterprises understand the value AI provides - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Startup Ascerta collects $18M in funding to help enterprises understand the value AI provides
Many businesses are spending enormous sums of money on artificial intelligence, but they don’t have any way to understand how much value those investments are returning — and that’s a challenge that a startup called Ascerta Inc. wants to solve after raising $18 million in an early-stage round of funding today.
Today’s Series A round was led by Dell Technologies Capital and saw participation from Hitachi Ventures, BGV and Wipro Ventures, bringing the startup’s total funding to date to $22.9 million.
Ascerta’s goal is to help businesses maximize their return on investment in AI, which is something that has proved to be a major challenge. Though most companies have no trouble counting their token consumption and measuring how many lines of AI-generated code they’ve generated, few are able to answer the very simple question: Which AI projects are actually creating value and making us money?
With traditional software, most companies were able to answer this question with basic financial operations or FinOps tools that shed light on how much they’re spending on things like cloud infrastructure resources. However, these tools aren’t very useful when it comes to trying to understand the real-world business outcomes achieved by an AI agent or coding assistant, said Ascerta co-founder and Chief Executive David Tepper.
According to Tepper, the only thing that most businesses see is “meaningless vanity metrics,” counting things like token consumption and agent runs. “They’re struggling to derive the real impact AI has on their business,” he explained. “We built Ascerta to cut through the noise and give organizations the means to win in the AI-era with insights specific to their business, people and use cases.”
Ascerta provides that guidance through a single, unified system that reveals exactly how a company is using AI, what the AI is doing and whether those efforts are translating into real revenue or savings. Its platform can connect to all of the most popular enterprise-grade AI tools, such as Microsoft Corp.’s CoConvoypilot, Anthropic PBC’s Claude, Amazon Web Services Inc.’s Bedrock and Salesforce Inc.’s Agentforce platform.
Once connected, it tracks the economics of AI down to the individual users, teams and applications. It can even unmask the hidden fees, enterprise discounts and sub-token costs missed by other tools, Tepper promised. “[We provide] purpose-built tools to prevent waste and aggressively optimize AI for value,” he said.
There are three specific components of Ascerta’s platform. Atlas measures AI adoption, the value it generates and its return on investment. Forge provides insights into how engineering teams are using coding agents and how they affect their productivity. Finally, Convoy helps companies to understand how much computing resources they’re using for AI, so they can consolidate workloads and optimize where possible without disrupting their business operations.
Ascerta has already helped companies like Atos SE and Wipro Ltd. to reap the rewards of their early AI investments, improving their return on investment by an average of 47% while reducing AI agent launch times by 24% and cutting wasted AI resource spending by 86%. Atos Group Chief AI Officer Florin Ratar said Ascerta’s platform has been “instrumental” in helping his company to scale its Sovereign Agentic Studios initiative, providing it with “visibility and control.”
Ramana Khanna, managing director of Dell Technologies Capital, said he’s backing Ascerta because it’s building a system of record for AI value creation. “Most enterprises are moving beyond broad AI experimentation and focusing their investments on what delivers measurable business value,” he said. “Ascerta is giving leaders the visibility and rigor they need to understand what’s working, optimize spending and scale their most successful AI initiatives.”

articles.title: El iPhone Duo ya tiene fecha para iniciar sus reservas: cuándo estará disponible
articles.text:
Apple permitirá que los usuarios se preparen para reservar el iPhone Duo a partir del lunes 12 de octubre, cuatro días antes de que comience la preventa oficial. El procedimiento estará disponible a través de la aplicación Apple Store y la página web de la compañía, donde los compradores podrán elegir anticipadamente el color, la capacidad de almacenamiento, el operador telefónico y el método de pago.
Cómo preparar la reserva del iPhone Duo antes de la preventa
Apple habilitará el proceso de preparación el lunes 12 de octubre. Desde esa fecha, los interesados podrán ingresar a la aplicación Apple Store o a la tienda en línea para configurar su pedido antes de que comience oficialmente la preventa.
PUBLICIDAD
El procedimiento permitirá seleccionar el color del iPhone Duo, la capacidad de almacenamiento y el operador de telefonía móvil, además de establecer el método de pago y completar otros datos necesarios para la compra.
Esta opción busca reducir el tiempo que los usuarios necesitan para realizar el pedido cuando se habilite la preventa. En lugar de comenzar desde cero el viernes 16 de octubre, quienes hayan completado los pasos previos solo tendrán que revisar y confirmar su compra.
La preparación estará disponible hasta antes del inicio de los pedidos anticipados, previsto para el viernes 16 de octubre. Apple suele ofrecer este mecanismo cuando presenta nuevos modelos de iPhone, especialmente aquellos que generan un elevado interés entre los compradores.
PUBLICIDAD
A qué hora comienza la preventa del iPhone Duo en Latinoamérica y España
Apple confirmó que los pedidos anticipados del iPhone Duo comenzarán el viernes 16 de octubre a las 8:00 a. m., hora del este de Estados Unidos (ET), y a las 5:00 a. m. en la costa del Pacífico (PT).
Para los compradores de otros países, estos son los horarios correspondientes al inicio de la preventa:
- Perú y Colombia: 7:00 a. m.
- México (Ciudad de México): 6:00 a. m.
- Argentina: 9:00 a. m.
- Chile: 9:00 a. m.
- España peninsular: 2:00 p. m.
- Estados Unidos (costa este): 8:00 a. m.
- Estados Unidos (costa del Pacífico): 5:00 a. m.
Estos horarios corresponden al comienzo de los pedidos anticipados y no necesariamente a la disponibilidad del dispositivo en todos los mercados. La fecha y las condiciones de venta pueden variar según el país.
Por qué conviene preparar el pedido antes del 16 de octubre
La posibilidad de configurar anticipadamente la compra puede resultar útil para quienes desean recibir el iPhone Duo desde el primer día de disponibilidad. Al tener seleccionadas las características del dispositivo y los datos de pago, los compradores podrán completar el proceso con menos pasos cuando se habilite la preventa.
PUBLICIDAD
Además, realizar la preparación con antelación permite revisar las opciones disponibles y evitar errores al momento de confirmar el pedido. Esto cobra importancia cuando se trata de un nuevo modelo que puede generar una elevada demanda durante sus primeras semanas en el mercado.
Apple recomienda utilizar este procedimiento a quienes tengan previsto comprar directamente en sus canales oficiales. Sin embargo, completar la preparación no garantiza una entrega en la fecha de lanzamiento, ya que los plazos dependerán de la disponibilidad del dispositivo y de las condiciones de cada mercado.
Con este sistema, la compañía busca agilizar el proceso de compra de su primer teléfono plegable y facilitar que los interesados completen sus pedidos desde el momento en que se abra la preventa.
