articles.title: A jury found Facebook guilty of 43 million privacy violations, and Meta could owe billions
articles.text:
Ripple effect: Cambridge Analytica is long gone, but Meta's social networks will likely suffer from the consequences for years to come. A New Mexico jury found the company guilty of millions of UPA violations, which means Mark Zuckerberg's mega-corporation should now prepare to write a rather generous check.
The New Mexico Department of Justice recently announced a landmark decision from the jury in the State of New Mexico v. Facebook, Inc. case. Meta's social network was found guilty of violating the New Mexico Unfair Practices Act (UPA) more than 43 million times, providing misleading statements to local consumers about the company's data practices.
The trial was related to the Cambridge Analytica (CA) scandal, one of the biggest privacy-violation cases in recent history. Meta settled the CA class action years ago, while the British consulting company went bankrupt almost ten years ago. But privacy abuses perpetrated by the consulting firm are still haunting Meta's business.
New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez said the verdict will act as a reminder that rules apply to everyone, even Facebook and other Big Tech players. The jury's decision might have a significant impact on both New Mexico and other states still trying to hold Big Tech accountable.
According to the jury's decision, Facebook lied to New Mexico netizens about how the company was managing their personal data. The network lied about its business practices with third-party companies, engaging in unfair and deceptive practices that allowed advertisers to easily access users' data. Furthermore, Facebook violated the UPA by profiting from misinformation and hate speech, while stating that it was actively removing or combating this kind of malicious content.
Facebook even lied in the statements following its internal investigation into Cambridge Analytica, the jury found. The social network had said it would probe third-party apps about their user data practices, conduct forensic audits, and more. The company apparently failed to fulfill its stated commitments.
After the jury's verdict, the judge is now required to decide how much Facebook will have to pay for the 43 million UPA violations. State authorities are looking to punish the company with the maximum civil penalty, which can be as high as $5,000 for each violation. Facebook might eventually be forced to pay the state of New Mexico billions of dollars.
Meta's reaction to the verdict was fairly predictable. A company spokesperson said that Meta's platforms are protected by First Amendment rights, which should cover free speech and users' rights over their data. The jury's decision apparently goes against this right, and Facebook will try to defend itself "against efforts to distort our record."
The Cambridge Analytica verdict comes a few months after Facebook lost another landmark case in New Mexico. In that particular case, a jury found the social network guilty of operating a service designed to hook younger users on the platform.

articles.title: ‘This is how AI should be used’ — OpenAI head of hardware breaks down the AI-assisted design of its Jalapeño ASIC
articles.text:
‘This is how AI should be used’ — OpenAI head of hardware breaks down the AI-assisted design of its Jalapeño ASIC
OpenAI cut typical development timelines in half, and the industry has already come knocking to understand how.
OpenAI’s Jalapeño ASIC is a seismic shift for the industry, not because of its efficiency or performance, but because of how it was designed. The company was clear from the jump that AI played a big role in the design process of Jalapeño, not only for the hardware itself, but also in the co-design with OpenAI’s software stack, allowing the ASIC to go from initial register-transfer level (RTL) to tapeout in a matter of just nine months. From concept to reveal, the timeline was less than two years. Richard Ho, head of hardware at OpenAI, says the timeline “established a new baseline,” and that the industry is already knocking on OpenAI’s door to learn how the company pulled it off.
“The way I like to think about it is, we’ve established a new baseline. In the old baseline, you’re talking 18 months to two years, roughly. Often that’s even with some existing IP or some more legacy architecture design,” Ho told Tom’s Hardware Premium in an interview. “We’re starting from scratch here. We had nothing. There’s not a line of code here to refer to. What we’ve established is that there’s a new baseline that you can do with a very talented team with the help of AI. Now, does it get shorter? It depends on what you’re trying to do.”
AI usage in chip design is nothing new, predating the era of LLMs entirely. The largest Electronic Design Automation (EDA) companies, Cadence and Synopsys, have a portfolio of AI-assisted chip design tools that have been around for several years. The models OpenAI used were its own internal models, however, and it leveraged both existing EDA tools and its new AI-assisted engineering workflow.
The engineering team used OpenAI’s agentic coding platform, Codex, for the Jalapeño design. “But we think that every engineering team in chip design should be able to use this as a new baseline, because it’s a proof point that the models that are in use — the AI models for us is mostly Codex, Sol, the one before Sol, and now we’re moving on to Astra. These are super capable. Even from when we started that work, back in November 2025, to when we taped out, the models improved enormously. Even from that moment to when we started doing the kernel optimization in May, when the chips were first coming online, we ourselves were shocked at how much better Codex was and what it could do,” Ho said.
Although AI was used during the entire development process, not only for design itself but also in writing and optimizing kernels, Ho continually reiterated the importance of talented engineers guiding those systems. The development story of Jalapeño is one of the few clear examples of AI bolstering a team of human workers, not displacing them.
Ho described the development cycle as a “good model” of how engineering teams should operate in the AI era. “This is how AI should be used. We didn’t replace our engineers; they just became super productive. With a smaller team of really good engineers with a lot of this AI stuff, you could do things faster and better than you could otherwise. I think that’s a good model of how engineering should be approached in the AI age.”
Although OpenAI managed to get working silicon much faster than a traditional development cycle, it wasn’t free of issues. For starters, OpenAI’s B0 stepping of Jalapeño reportedly delivers up to a 25% improvement in performance per watt over the original A0 stepping. That’s closer to a generational improvement than stepping optimization, suggesting that, at least for a brand new hardware team, there may have been design oversights with the original stepping. Attributing that to AI or humans is anyone’s guess.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Other frontier labs are circling for a slice of the pie, as well. Clive Chan, a key engineer on Jalapeño and the second-ever hardware hire at OpenAI, left the company in June to join the hardware team at Anthropic. Ho says there’s already been “a lot of interest in the industry” for OpenAI’s AI-assisted chip design process, and says that “we’ll see more about that quite shortly.”
“I’m not going to preempt anything here. I can tell you that there’s a lot of interest in the industry, and I would also tell you that we feel that there is a lot of benefit in industry generally that we want to enable,” Ho said. “I think that’s something that we’ll see more about quite shortly, to be honest.”
Ho referenced the dozens of AI-first chip design startups in Silicon Valley, suggesting OpenAI may eventually introduce tools of its own to aid other firms with AI chip development. “We have our take on that, and I think at some point we want to tell the world, “Here’s our take on it.” Fundamental to that is Codex and GPT-6 Astra coming out. Those are fundamental, and we can basically point to it; it’s not going to be slideware or vaporware. We can point to it and say, “Here’s what we did, here’s how we did it, and here’s what we got.” It’s going to be very concrete.”
What exactly the “it” Ho is referring to here remains a mystery, though given the context, it sounds like OpenAI may explore some way to productize its AI chip design workflow. Ho says Astra is a big step toward that, and we’ve already seen the model in action performing impressive feats, such as completing Portal autonomously.
Although OpenAI leveraged its own models heavily for Jalapeño's design and validation, it didn’t completely break the mold of traditional EDA workflows, particularly at the end of the design process. Before tapeout, tools from companies like Synopsys and Cadence perform a series of tests for signoff, including static timing analysis and signal integrity analysis. Ho says that OpenAI used this typical EDA flow for Jalapeño.
“But for sign-off, you need to use the standard EDA flows, and we did, because you want to make sure those results are good and correct. There’s no real alternative today. Part of it is this combination of standard flows optimized with AI, optimized by really good engineers,” Ho said.
OpenAI shared a multi-generational roadmap for accelerators. It says its second-gen ASIC is approaching tape-out, and its third generation is already in development. Although Ho said that the Jalapeño development cycle establishes a new baseline for chip design timelines, he was cautious about calling that cycle and cadence.
“Our projects and tape-outs will be dependent on the maturity level of the technologies. We can do very fast execution. Will we do those types of executions back-to-back? I doubt it, because the technology will not be ready for that, and I don’t want to tape out something that is 2% better than what I taped out before, because it’s not worth it to change a fleet,” Ho told us.
The executive was also clear that the Jalapeño timeline isn’t necessarily the same timeline all chips will follow. There were some “pragmatic trade-offs” in the early architecture design, with the team avoiding emerging, complex design points like 3D stacking and co-packaged optics. “Will it take longer? Will it take nine months? I won't say it will take nine months… but I think it will go faster than if you didn't have AI models.” 
You can read the full transcript of the interview, which covers a wide range of topics, at Tom's Hardware Premium.

articles.title: The ugly economics of consumer AI | TechCrunch
articles.text:
After this week, you could argue that consumer AI is making a comeback.
Meta’s personal AI assistant, Muse, and its plush-like mascot Jolly, has been a surprise hit. OpenAI’s Dots, released just yesterday, appears to be chasing the same cartoony personal assistant idea. And the up-and-coming Instinct assistant reached a $10 billion valuation on the strength of its agentic errand-running, focused on booking travel, making restaurant reservations, or cancelling subscriptions.
The bull case is easy to make. Agentic AI has finally gotten reliable enough to handle everyday tasks. Companies are increasingly pitching that service to everyday people, who are getting genuine value out of it. If you’re an investor, that looks an awful lot like the ChatGPT launch in 2022 — the raw power of AI opening up a product category that was never possible before. Who wouldn’t want a piece of the action?
But there’s a reason frontier labs have gotten gun-shy about consumer AI — and it’s not because the tech isn’t good enough. Even staggeringly popular tech products are starting to hit a ceiling on how much money consumers are willing to pay, and it’s not clear that better models are actually leading to a more profitable consumer business. The result has been an industry-wide shift toward the Anthropic model, focusing on enterprise contracts and vertical-by-vertical expansion.
If products like Muse and Instinct are bucking that trend, it’s because they’re less concerned with monetization. But the underlying economics of consumer AI are not getting any better, and anyone getting into the business will have to grapple with them eventually.
We got a reminder of those economics in Andreessen Horowitz’s semiannual State of Markets report, which pulled its figures from a PNC research report from this summer. In two charts, they track the slowly growing percentage of consumers paying for AI services, alongside the slowly growing amount they’re paying. As of May, 2.2% of consumers were paying for AI, at an average spend of $31 a month.
Andreessen puts a positive spin on this, saying, “it’s still so early when it comes to mature AI adoption and utilization.” There’s a lot of room to grow! But in both charts, the pace of growth seems awfully linear. Even as models make huge improvements, there isn’t a ton of movement in the number of customers willing to pay for AI or how much they’re willing to pay for it. The enormous performance jump from GPT-5.2 to Astra, for instance, is barely visible on the chart.
The per-consumer numbers are less striking, but still far below the standard break-even point. If you take Netflix as the standard for market-saturated online services (at 325 million subscribers), then $34 per customer only gets you to $11 billion in annual revenue, less than a third of OpenAI’s operating costs.
If you think PNC is underselling adoption, you can get similar numbers from Bank of America. In March, the firm found that roughly 3% of U.S. consumers paid for AI, up 40% from the previous year. A Menlo survey from September gives a slightly sunnier view, finding that a quarter of adults use AI daily and half of those users are paying for it.
The problem with the consumer approach has less to do with revenue than with cost. AI is an unusually expensive technology to operate, particularly compared to lightweight predecessors like social networking or cloud computing. Even hundreds of millions of paying customers doesn’t guarantee you’ll break even.
To its credit, OpenAI seems to have adapted well to these facts. The company’s widely reported pivot to enterprise has been largely successful, with enterprise bookings reportedly doubling since July. Even the Dots launch had a strong enterprise angle, showing how the new personal agent could be useful for software engineers and agency creatives. One long-standing way to make money from popular-but-cheap consumer services is to sell them to businesses at a markup, and OpenAI seems to be following the playbook.
It’s harder to say what this means for Muse and Instinct. Muse has the juggernaut of Meta’s personalized ad targeting behind it, which gives it more options for monetization and more time before it becomes an urgent question. Notably, Meta is already exploring the enterprise angle.
Instinct has a separate plan that involves taking a cut of purchases made through the agent, which might raise the ceiling. Presumably it’ll also be able to avoid the cost of training a frontier model, which will help a lot.
But the ugly economics of consumer AI put a hard cap on how large the company can plausibly grow without tapping into enterprise revenue. It’s a lesson the major labs have already learned, and it’s one of the few things about the industry that doesn’t seem to be changing.

articles.title: Reddit says it has to cut back access to ‘Old Reddit’ because of AI bots
articles.text:
Reddit is further limiting who can use the “Old Reddit” experience as part of its efforts to combat scraping and automated traffic. Reddit recently started forcing users to log in to be able to use Old Reddit, but in the “next few months,” the company says that you’ll have to be logged in and have used Old Reddit within the last six months from when the change rolls out to be able to continue browsing the platform with the classic experience.
Reddit says it has to cut back access to ‘Old Reddit’ because of AI bots
Viewing the old Reddit UI will get even harder if you’re not a mod, now that it’s only available to accounts that have used it recently.
Reddit says the six-month window covers “the vast majority of all Old Reddit users.” The announcement didn’t go into detail, but it’s clearly aimed at blocking not just new account creation for bots, but also any bots that might access unused or abandoned accounts. As part of the changes, Reddit will stop supporting RSS feeds on November 13th because RSS is “now a common surface for large-scale scraping and automated abuse,” and suggested replacements like Discord Relay for moderation help.
Reddit:
If you use RSS for feeds outside of a community you moderate, there is no replacement. We know RSS has been a beloved part of the open web for a long time, and we’re grateful to everyone who used it to stay connected to Reddit.
The company has been waging war against unsanctioned access to its data for some time, including blocking the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine to prevent AI scraping, suing Anthropic over alleged unauthorized bot access, and striking deals with Google and OpenAI to use Reddit data for training. Reddit knows that Old Reddit is beloved by many users, and in May 2025, CEO Steve Huffman said the company would “keep it online as long as people are using it.” But this past August, Huffman said that Reddit had gotten to a point where “we need to make some changes” because the experience was being used by “everyone who spams, scrapes, or does anything bad on Reddit.”
In its announcement today, Reddit said that the recent login requirement for Old Reddit “helped reduce scraping and automated abuse” but “still allowed any logged-in account to access Old Reddit, including accounts with no prior Old Reddit use.” Logged-in moderators, however, will still be able to use Old Reddit without a recent usage requirement.
Reddit also shared updates for the previously announced transition moving apps and bots that use Reddit’s public data API to the company’s developer platform. Reddit will begin removing API access for users that haven’t registered their apps by January 12th, 2027, and all remaining public API access “will end in March 2027.”

articles.title: Samsung presenta las tablets más interesantes para la IA: así son las Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra y Galaxy Tab S12+
articles.text:
Samsung es uno de los fabricantes que históricamente más ha apostado por el segmento de las tablets Android. Ahora la compañía reafirma su postura con la presentación de la nueva Galaxy Tab S12, una nueva generación de sus tablets que sigue haciendo gala de un diseño tremendamente fino pero resistente, buena batería y, como en el caso de sus smartphones, cargada de funciones con IA.
En esta ocasión, la nueva tablet de Samsung llega en dos versiones, Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra y Galaxy Tab S12+, ambas compatibles con el S Pen, y cuya diferencia más representativa es su tamaño: 14.6 pulgadas en la Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra y 12.6 pulgadas en la Galaxy Tab S12+, ambas con 120 Hz de tasa de refresco, Dynamic AMOLED 2X y hasta un brillo máximo de 1,600 nits.
Además, en su interior no encontramos un Exynos de Samsung, sino un MediaTek Dimensity 9500 complementado con opciones 16GB + 1TB, 12GB + 512GB, 12GB + 256GB, microSD de hasta 2TB en el caso de la Ultra y 12GB + 512GB, 12GB + 256GB.
microSD de hasta 2 TB en el caso de la Tab S12+. Ambas incluyen certificación IP68 y lector de huellas en pantalla.
Y respecto a su precio y disponibilidad, Samsung ha confirmado que la Galaxy Tab S12 estará disponible en España a partir del 7 de octubre en color gris, a partir de 1.299€ en función de la capacidad elegida. Por su parte, la Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra arrancará desde 1.539 €.
Además, la compañía asegura que, respecto a su longevidad en el futuro, ambos modelos tendrán hasta siete generaciones de actualizaciones del sistema operativo y parches de seguridad.
Nueva generación del SmartTag
Junto con las Galaxy Tab S12, Samsung también ha presentado la nueva generación de su dispositivo rastreador: Galaxy SmartTag3. La nueva generación ofrece un diseño que es un 35% más pequeño tanto en volumen como un 33% más ligero que los modelos anteriores.
Tiene una forma redondeada y un acabado en aluminio que lo hace ideal para colocarlo incluso en los lugares más insospechados, y esta vez es totalmente compatible entre distintos sistemas operativos, incluyendo iOS.
Cuenta con Bluetooth 6.0 Channel Sounding, tecnología de banda ultraancha (UWB) y es compatible con Galaxy Find Network y sus 900 millones de dispositivos Galaxy Respecto a su autonomía, el SmartTag3 ofrece hasta 550 días con un uso estándar y de hasta 790 días en el modo de ahorro de energía.
El Samsung Galaxy SmartTag3 estará disponible en España próximamente en los colores blanco y negro, aunque todavía no se conoce su precio.

articles.title: Still haven't got the fancy new Start menu in Windows 11? Microsoft's 26H2 update has arrived and installing it could trigger any delayed upgrades
articles.text:
'Uh oh': Windows 11 26H2 is here and Microsoft says it's a 'predictable and low-disruption update', but a lot of people are preparing for the worst
A minor update, but one that could push through new features from earlier this year
- Windows 11 26H2 is here and Microsoft says it's a "predictable and low-disruption update"
- There are users on social media who very much disagree, and are expressing their nervousness in varying degrees
- However, the 26H2 update could trigger the rollout of features that your PC hasn't yet received, so it might prove very useful
Windows 11's annual update has arrived, and while 26H2 doesn't bring in notable new features, it should trigger the rollout of functionality from earlier this year – if you still don't have some of those bits and pieces.
As Microsoft explains: "Windows 11 version 26H2 … delivers the latest Windows innovations with a streamlined update experience designed to minimize disruption and help you stay secure, productive, and up to date."
As with last year's update, this is what Microsoft calls a "small enablement package", meaning it's a minimal download with a quick installation that happens in a single reboot. All it's effectively doing is flicking a switch to turn on some preloaded code, with no actual new features delivered as such.
There's a key point to note here though, because as Microsoft says, this update "activates new features already included in the operating system through previous monthly servicing updates."
So, if you haven't yet had a feature rolled out to you – such as Microsoft's change to more speedily load apps, or the ability to reposition the taskbar, or the various changes for the Start menu – applying the 26H2 update should ensure that anything missing reaches your PC.
It's also worth bearing in mind that installing a new version of Windows 11 extends your support timeframe (through to October 2028 in the case of 26H2).
Analysis: skeptics aplenty
I say that installing version 26H2 should mean that any missing Windows 11 features are enabled on your PC, because obviously there's no guarantee, but if you've been hankering after a particular piece of functionality, there's a good chance you'll get it by applying this upgrade (certainly with older features, anyway).
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
As ever, though, it's never a great idea to rush to download any update, at least in my opinion, because of the danger that some unforeseen bug has crept in. Microsoft talks about this update being small and "designed to minimize disruption", and it should be a clean enough installation in theory, but people have been burned before – and the reaction on Reddit shows that quite clearly.
Posting in response to Microsoft calling 26H2 a "predictable and low-disruption update", one Redditor summed up the broad feeling in the thread by saying: "Well, now I'm really suspicious." Another poster simply says: "Uh oh."
And there are countless jokes or sarcastic barbs about how 26H2 will be just great because AI coded it, such as: "Don't worry they told Copilot not to make any mistakes with this update."
Another Redditor takes a similar attitude to myself: "I'll wait 3 weeks and then see what the situation looks like before updating."
There's no need to jump right on this update, so it just seems prudent to hold fire for a short while and see if any annoying incidents happen that move the needle on the glitch-o-meter.
Let's hope not, and then at some point later in October, you can apply version 26H2 and with any luck you'll get any features that have missed out your PC in Microsoft's rollout schedule. Speaking of which, it's notable how many more folks are complaining about Windows 11 being very slow to deploy new capabilities this year, but that said, you can't exactly blame Microsoft for being cautious given that bugs remain a big problem for its desktop OS.
Slowing down to a treacly pace with feature rollouts isn't exactly an ideal solution, though, is it? Microsoft needs to address some more deep-seated issues with its testing processes here (and no, I won't shut up about this until something is actually seen to be happening at the company in this regard).

articles.title: Samsung presenta el nuevo Galaxy SmartTag3, un nuevo modelo más preciso, más pequeño y, por primera vez, compatible con iOS
articles.text:
Aunque quizás las nuevas Galaxy Tab han sido el lanzamiento más destacado de hoy de Samsung, no podemos obviar su nuevo localizador: el SmartTag3. Su antecesor, el SmartTag2, es uno de los mejores localizadores Android que hay a día de hoy, pese a llevar varios años en el mercado. Este nuevo modelo llega con un rediseño evidente, pero con una novedad que sobresale por encima de todas las demás: el nuevo dispositivo de Samsung ahora también es compatible con iOS. Llegará a España en los próximos meses, aunque de momento no tiene fecha.
Un localizador más compacto y con autonomía para hasta 550 días
Salta a la vista que el diseño de este nuevo localizador cambia con respecto al anterior SmartTag2. Este último era más grande y tenía un orificio para poder colocarlo en un llavero. Sin embargo, el nuevo SmartTag3 apuesta por un diseño más delgado y compacto, lo que lo hace más recomendable si buscas guardarlo en un pequeño bolsillo o en algún lugar que necesite un poco más de discreción. Es cierto que pierde el orificio para el llavero, pero esto es algo que podemos compensar adquiriendo un accesorio por separado.
Para la nueva versión, Samsung apuesta por Bluetooth 6.0 Channel Sounding, una tecnología que nos permitirá encontrar el localizador con la 'vista de brújula' con mucha precisión a una distancia de hasta 60 metros. También es compatible con UWB y se apoya en la llamada Galaxy Find Network, una red compuesta por más de 900 millones de nodos que permiten que la posición del localizador se vaya actualizando. Esos nodos son dispositivos Galaxy de todo el mundo.
A nivel de funciones, también tenemos novedades. Este localizador estrena 'Notificación de lugar', que nos permitirá establecer un área para recibir una notificación si el SmartTag la abandona. Esto es útil para saber, de manera instantánea, si nuestra mascota abandona el jardín de casa. También podremos configurarlo para recibir una notificación en caso de movimiento, así como consultar un historial de ubicaciones.
En cuanto a autonomía, Samsung promete que el localizador es capaz de aguantar hasta 550 días con un uso estándar y hasta 790 días si lo usamos en modo de ahorro de energía (utiliza una pila de botón CR2032). Como decimos, es el primer localizador de Samsung en ser compatible con iOS, aunque los usuarios de Apple no podrán acceder a todas sus funciones.

articles.title: La película de 'Juego de Tronos' de Aegon el Conquistador ya tiene director y fecha de estreno
articles.text:
La primera película de Juego de Tronos ya tiene fecha de estreno oficial. Warner Bros. está preparando un ambicioso proyecto antes de unirse definitivamente a Paramount, y lo harán con una de sus franquicias más importantes. Tras muchos años expandiéndose únicamente con series para HBO, la saga medieval de George R.R. Martin está lista para dar el salto a los cines.
Lo hará con una película live-action que será precuela de la serie original. Concretamente, el filme se centrará en Aegon Targaryen el Conquistador, uno de los personajes clave de todo el universo Juego de Tronos. Se trata del fundador de la dinastía Targaryen y unificador de seis de los Siete Reinos. Su historia es una de las más importantes de la saga y por fin podremos verla en pantalla.
Ahora, se ha desvelado que la película de Juego de Tronos sobre Aegon el Conquistador se estrenará en cines el 1 de junio de 2029. Además, también se ha confirmado que Owen Harris, quien ya ha trabajado en la serie El caballero de los Siete Reinos, será el director. El guion correrá a cargo del nominado al Oscar Beau Willimon, showrunner de House of Cards y guionista de Andor.
Quién fue Aegon el Conquistador
Aegon Targaryen fue el segundo hijo de Lord Aerion Targaryen y Lady Valaena Velaryon, los Señores de Rocadragón. Este era el título máximo que, por entonces, tenía la Casa Targaryen. Aegon tuvo una hermana mayor, Visneya, y una menor, Rhaenys, y se casó con ambas. Con la primera, por tradición valyria. Con la segunda, por amor.
Aegon Targaryen vivió y creció en la isla de Rocadragón, en el extremo más occidental de lo que antaño fue el Feudo Franco de Valyria, destruido casi un siglo antes en la Maldición de Valyria. Eventualmente, a sus 25 años, puso su vista en Poniente y en los Siete Reinos. Se dice que incluso pintó un mapa del continente en una mesa, pero sin fronteras, simbolizando toda su unión. Su plan era unificar los Siete Reinos y convertirse en el rey.
Date de alta en HBO MAX y tendrás acceso a las mejores series y películas exclusivas como The Wire, Los Soprano o Casa del Dragón. Incluye todo el catálogo de Warner, los clásicos de Cartoon Network, los grandes estrenos y el mejor deporte.
Junto a su enorme dragón Balerion (el más grande de todo Juego de Tronos) y los de sus hermanas/esposas, Vhagar (sí, el mismo de La Casa del Dragón) y Meraxes, lideró a sus ejércitos a una victoria tras otra. Así, consiguió lo que parecía impensable, conquistar todo Poniente a excepción de Dorne, que siempre resistió. Aun así, el Septón Supremo le ungió como Aegon de la Casa Targaryen, el primero de su nombre, Rey de los Ándalos y los Rhoynar y los Primeros Hombres, Señor de los Siete Reinos y Protector del Reino.

Alors qu’Amazon a officiellement pris rendez-vous pour ses Jours Flash Prime les 6 et 7 octobre prochains, le géant du e-commerce n’attend pas le coup d’envoi pour ouvrir le bal des promotions. On trouve déjà une première salve de rabais sur son catalogue tech. Voici notre sélection des meilleures offres anticipées à saisir dès aujourd’hui : uniquement pour les membres Prime.
Les meilleures offres Amazon en DIRECT
Navee GT3 Pro
La Navee GT3 Pro est une trottinette électrique taillée pour les trajets quotidiens exigeants : suspension quadruple, moteur puissant et jusqu’à 60 km d’autonomie en font un choix sérieux pour les navetteurs qui veulent rouler sans se soucier du revêtement.
- Autonomie annoncée jusqu’à 60 km avec gestion intelligente de la batterie
- Suspensions avant et arrière pour absorber les chocs sur terrain irrégulier
- Contrôle de traction (TCS) et double freinage pour plus de stabilité par temps glissant
La Navee GT3 Pro est disponible en promotion à 379,99 euros sur Amazon, au lieu de 549 euros habituellement.
VITURE Pro 2
Les lunettes XR VITURE Pro 2 projettent un écran virtuel de 146 pouces en 1080p à 120 Hz, compatible avec la plupart des appareils USB-C à sortie vidéo : Steam Deck, ROG Ally, iPhone 15 et 16, MacBook ou ordinateurs portables Windows. À 63 g, elles tiennent dans la poche et s’utilisent aussi bien dans l’avion que sur le canapé.
- Dalle Sony Micro-OLED, 1 600 nits de luminosité de pointe et HDR
- Optique UltraClarity 3.0 pour un texte net sur toute la surface de vision
- Application SpaceWalker gratuite pour plusieurs écrans virtuels et espace de travail élargi
Les VITURE Pro 2 sont disponibles en promotion à 329 euros sur Amazon, au lieu de 439 euros.
Dreame X60 Pro Ultra
Le Dreame X60 Pro Ultra est un robot aspirateur laveur haut de gamme qui repousse littéralement ses limites : sa technologie UltraExtend étend la brosse latérale jusqu’à 12 cm et la serpillière jusqu’à 18 cm pour atteindre les bords et les coins certifiés à 100 % par le TÜV SÜD. Il franchit aussi des seuils jusqu’à 10 cm, ce qui est franchement rare dans cette catégorie.
- Aspiration de 42 000 Pa avec brosse démêlante anti-poils jusqu’à 40 cm
- Lavage des sols à serpillière chaude (plus de 40 °C) pour les taches tenaces
- Autonettoyage des serpillières à 100 °C, séchage à l’air chaud intégré
Le Dreame X60 Pro Ultra est disponible en promotion à 1 099 euros sur Amazon, au lieu de 1 499 euros habituellement.
Fire TV Stick 4K (2026)
Amazon vient de sortir une nouvelle génération de son Fire TV Stick 4K. Une clé HDMI qui promet plus de réactivité et arrive avec une télécommande entièrement revue.
- Des applications qui se lancent 35 % plus vite, selon Amazon
- Une télécommande asymétrique, à la base lestée, facile à prendre en main
- Wi-Fi 6, 4K à 60 i/s et décodage AV1
Lancé à 74,99 euros, le Fire TV Stick 4K de 2026 est proposé en ce moment en promotion à 35,99 euros sur Amazon.
Anker Nano 45 W avec écran intelligent
Le Anker Nano 45 W est un chargeur compact équipé d’un écran qui affiche en temps réel la puissance de charge, avec un mode de protection batterie activable en deux pressions.
- Charge un iPhone 17 Pro de 0 à 50 % en 20 minutes
- Mode Anker Care : température de charge réduite de 5 °C
- 47 % plus compact que le chargeur 30 W Apple d’origine
Le Anker Nano 45 W est disponible à 27,99 € sur Amazon, au lieu de 39,99 €.
Anker Soundcore Q20i
Le Soundcore Q20i est un casque Bluetooth à réduction de bruit active proposé par Anker à moins de 30 euros : une entrée de gamme sérieuse pour qui veut s’isoler sans se ruiner. Avec 40 heures d’autonomie en mode ANC et une charge rapide, il fait clairement le taf pour les trajets quotidiens.
- ANC hybride à 4 micros, jusqu’à 90 % de réduction du bruit
- 40 heures d’autonomie avec ANC, 60 heures sans
- Multipoint Bluetooth 5.0 pour deux appareils simultanés
Le Soundcore Q20i est disponible en promotion à 28,99 euros sur Amazon, au lieu de 49,99 euros habituellement.
CREATE WINDCALM S
Le CREATE WINDCALM S est un ventilateur de plafond conçu pour fonctionner aussi bien en intérieur qu’en extérieur, équipé d’un moteur DC silencieux et d’un kit LED 15 W avec trois températures de couleur.
- Moteur DC ultra-silencieux, utilisable en intérieur et en extérieur
- Fonction été-hiver : inversion du sens de rotation pour redistribuer la chaleur
- Éclairage LED 15 W avec trois températures de couleur (chaude, neutre, froide)
Le CREATE WINDCALM S est disponible en promotion à 80,95 euros sur Amazon, au lieu de 95,95 euros habituellement.
EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max
La DELTA 2 Max est une station d’énergie portable conçue pour alimenter la quasi-totalité des appareils du foyer, avec une capacité de base de 2 kWh extensible jusqu’à 6 kWh en ajoutant des batteries supplémentaires.
- Recharge complète en 81 minutes via la prise secteur (2 300 W)
- Batterie LFP avec 3 000 cycles de charge, garantie 5 ans
- 13 sorties pour alimenter jusqu’à 3 100 W en mode X-Boost
La EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max est disponible à 899 euros sur Amazon, au lieu de 999 euros habituellement.
Voici d’autres offres Prime anticipées sur Amazon
- Anker Nano Chargeur USB C à 27 euros au lieu de 39 euros
- Nebula Capsule 3 Laser Mini à 479 euros au lieu de 699 euros
- Eufy Smart Scale P3 à 49 euros au lieu de 89 euros
- EZVIZ DL01 Pro à 139 euros au lieu de 179 euros
- Dreame A1 Pro à 699 euros au lieu de 1 099 euros
- Ninja Foodi FlexDrawer à 179 euros au lieu de 219 euros
Anker Nano Chargeur USB C
Parfait pour faire le plein d’énergie en un éclair et sans encombrement, le chargeur Anker Nano de 45W avec son petit écran intégré coûte moins de 30 euros grâce à cette offre.
Les points forts du Anker Nano
- Un chargeur compact avec écran intégré
- Une puissance de 45W
- Un port USB-C
De base à 39 euros, le chargeur USB-C Anker Nano est aujourd’hui remisé à 27,99 euros sur Amazon.
Nebula Capsule 3 Laser Mini
C’est un vidéoprojecteur qui cumule les atouts : batterie intégrée, format canette, projection d’images en Full HD jusqu’à 120 pouces… Si sa version LED était déjà recommandable, le modèle Laser l’est encore plus, puisqu’il parvient à proposer des contrastes plus marqués et une meilleure luminosité. Bonne nouvelle : il est à -31 %.
Le Nebula Capsule 3 Laser Mini en résumé
- Un format ultra-compact bien pratique
- Des images en Full HD jusqu’à 120 pouces, avec de beaux contrastes
- Google TV intégré
Au lieu d’un prix barré à 699 euros, le Nebula Capsule 3 Laser Mini est aujourd’hui remisé à 479 euros sur le site d’Amazon.
Eufy Smart Scale P3
Garder un œil sur sa santé ne nécessite plus de vider son compte en banque. La balance connectée eufy Smart Scale P3 profite d’une belle promotion. Suivi complet de 16 métriques corporelles, écran couleur personnalisable et synchronisation Wi-Fi : un équipement ultra-complet pour suivre vos objectifs de remise en forme sans vous prendre la tête.
Les atouts de l’Eufy P3
- Un écran en couleur
- Suivi de santé complet avec 16 indicateurs de santé
- Reconnaissance automatique de chaque membre de la famille
De base, la balance connectée d’Eufy P3 est proposée à 89 euros, mais grâce à cette offre Prime anticipée, elle chute à 49 euros sur Amazon.
EZVIZ DL01 Pro
Le kit Ezviz DL01 Pro vous permet d’ouvrir et de fermer votre porte sans clé, mais avec votre smartphone ou un digicode qui s’installe très facilement. Actuellement, ce pack est proposé à moins de 140 euros.
Pourquoi choisir l’EZVIZ DL01 Pro ?
- Une serrure intelligente facile à installer
- Le déverrouillage de la porte depuis un smartphone ou avec le clavier fourni
- Un clavier, des badges…
L’EZVIZ DL01 Pro est actuellement en promotion à 139 euros sur Amazon au lieu de 179 euros habituellement.
Dreame A1 Pro
Le Dreame A1 Pro est une version évoluée du Dreame A1 qui s’occupe de votre jardin sans aucun câble périphérique. C’est un robot tondeuse autonome qui cartographie votre jardin, identifie les obstacles et les massifs à ne pas ratiboiser. Le tout piloté par une application qui représente le seul effort que vous aurez à faire. En ce moment, il coûte 36 % de moins.
Les forces du Dreame A1 Pro
- Une installation sans fil ni balise en 30 min max
- Le capteur LiDAR 3D pour une navigation autonome
- Ses roues crantées pour des pentes à 45 %
Lancé à 1 099 euros, le robot tondeuse Dreame A1 Pro est en ce moment remisé à 699 euros sur le site d’Amazon.
Ninja Foodi FlexDrawer
Le Ninja Foodi FlexDrawer est un Air Fryer qui permet de cuisiner deux plats différents de façon simultanée, grâce aux deux zones de cuisson dans la grande cuve. En ce moment, on le trouve à moins de 180 euros.
Les avantages du Ninja Foodi FlexDrawer
- Une cuve qui peut être séparée en deux compartiments de cuisson
- Une capacité de 10,4 L
- Sept programmes de cuisson
Le Ninja Foodi FlexDrawer coûte 269 euros, mais en ce moment sur Amazon, l’Air Fryer revient à seulement 179 euros sur Amazon.

articles.title: Amazon brade sa Kindle 2024 à moins de 90 € avant l'arrivée de sa remplaçante
articles.text:
La relève de la Kindle d’entrée de gamme se précise. Le 28 septembre, le site allemand WinFuture a publié des images présentées comme officielles de la 12e génération de la liseuse (les visuels sont détaillés sur Frandroid). On y voit un écran aux coins arrondis, un bouton d’alimentation qui passe du bas de la liseuse au haut de la tranche droite, et quatre coloris : noir, bleu clair, vert et violet. Amazon n’a encore rien confirmé et aucune date de sortie n’a filtré.
En attendant, Amazon fait de la place dans ses rayons. La Kindle 2024 passe à 89,99 € au lieu de 154,99 € dans sa version avec publicités, soit 65 € d’économie. La promotion tombe en pleine rentrée littéraire, au moment où les soirées raccourcissent.
Il faut quand même relativiser ce « prix de référence ». À sa sortie fin 2024, la Kindle 2024 coûtait 109,99 € dans sa version avec publicités. Elle est brièvement passée à 154,99 € début septembre (169,99 € sans publicités). Par rapport à son prix de lancement, la remise est donc de 20 €.
Que vaut la Kindle 2024 ?
La Kindle 2024 est la liseuse la plus simple de la gamme d’Amazon. Elle a un écran de 6 pouces à encre électronique (E Ink), une technologie qui reflète la lumière comme une page imprimée et ne consomme de l’énergie qu’au moment où la page change. Sa résolution de 300 pixels par pouce, la même que sur les modèles plus chers, donne un texte net, sans effet de flou autour des lettres. Un éclairage avant réglable permet de lire dans le noir, et un mode sombre affiche le texte en blanc sur fond noir.
Elle est équipée de 16 Go de stockage, de quoi garder des milliers de livres. Le Bluetooth sert à écouter des livres audio avec un casque ou une enceinte sans fil. Amazon annonce jusqu’à six semaines d’autonomie, sur la base d’une demi-heure de lecture par jour avec le Wi-Fi coupé. La recharge passe par un port USB-C et prend environ deux heures avec un adaptateur secteur de 9 W, vendu à part.
La liseuse pèse 158 g pour 8 mm d’épaisseur, de quoi la glisser dans la poche d’un manteau. Elle a quand même quelques limites. Elle n’est pas étanche, donc on évite la lecture dans le bain. Son éclairage reste en lumière froide, sans réglage de teinte plus chaude pour le soir. Le bouton d’alimentation est placé sur la tranche inférieure, à un endroit peu pratique, et c’est justement ce que la prochaine génération semble corriger. Les fichiers EPUB, enfin, doivent passer par le service d’envoi d’Amazon pour être lus.
À ce prix, la Kindle 2024 est-elle une bonne affaire ?
D’après les images qui ont fuité, la nouvelle génération changerait surtout de look. Elle garderait un écran d’environ 6 pouces, aux coins arrondis et peut-être avec un éclairage un peu plus puissant, selon WinFuture. Son prix reste inconnu. Si vous cherchez avant tout une liseuse pour lire des romans, le modèle actuel en fait déjà l’essentiel.
Rien ne garantit en revanche que cette remise dure jusqu’à l’annonce officielle, ni que les stocks tiennent. Amazon n’a communiqué ni le prix ni la date de sortie de la 12e génération. À 89,99 €, la Kindle 2024 permet de se constituer une première bibliothèque numérique sans l’attendre.

articles.title: Microsoft: Warum sich Windows fast jeden USB-Speicher merkt, den du jemals angeschlossen hast
articles.text:
Microsoft: Warum sich Windows fast jeden USB-Speicher merkt, den du jemals angeschlossen hast
Was macht Windows, wenn du ein USB-Gerät an deinen Computer anschließt? Es merkt es sich – und das bereits seit mindestens 14 Jahren.
Nicht nur der Gerätename wird gespeichert
Schon 2012 schrieb Jason Walker, ein „Premier Field Engineer“ bei Microsoft, im Scripting-Blog des US-Unternehmens: „Wenn ein USB-Speichergerät an einen Computer angeschlossen wird, wird in der Registrierung der Schlüssel ‚USBSTOR‘ erstellt. Dieser Schlüssel enthält alle Informationen, die das Betriebssystem über das jeweilige Speichergerät benötigt.“
Warum macht Windows das? Und welche Informationen speichert es über angeschlossene USB-Laufwerke? Windows Latest hat sich genauer mit diesen Fragen beschäftigt. Sie kommt zum Ergebnis, dass der Gerätename zusammen mit Hardware- und Instanzkennungen, die aus den vom Gerät übermittelten Informationen abgeleitet werden, gespeichert werden.
Einträge enthalten keine Liste der auf dem Laufwerk gespeicherten Dateien
Je nach Gerät kann die Instanzkennung etwa Informationen zur Seriennummer enthalten, sowie Daten darüber, wann das Laufwerk erstmals eingerichtet, wann es zuletzt angeschlossen oder entfernt wurde und welchen Laufwerksbuchstaben es zugewiesen bekam. Eine weitere Erkenntnis lautet: „Tastaturen, Webcams, USB-Mäuse oder USB-Mikrofone tauchen in USBSTOR nicht auf.“
Die USBSTOR-Einträge enthalten laut Windows Latest „jedoch keine Liste der auf dem Laufwerk gespeicherten Dateien“. Sie können demnach lediglich zeigen, dass Windows ein bestimmtes Gerät erkannt hat. Sie allein würden keinen Aufschluss darüber geben, welche Dateien kopiert wurden, ob Daten auf das Gerät übertragen oder davon abgerufen wurden oder wer das Gerät physisch angeschlossen hat.
Auch Linux und macOS speichern solche Daten
Laut Windows Latest speichern auch Linux und macOS Geräteinformationen und Systemprotokolle zur Hardware: „Diese Betriebssysteme müssen Hardware identifizieren, die passenden Treiber laden und bei Problemen die Fehlersuche unterstützen.“
Das Fazit des Portals: Das Ganze wirke weitaus bedenklicher (dabei spielt es auf „panikmachende“ Beiträge über Windows in den sozialen Medien an), als es eigentlich ist.

articles.title: Karnataka approves Global Technology Centres in Belagavi and Hubballi
articles.text:
Karnataka approves Global Technology Centres in Belagavi and Hubballi
Karnataka approves Global Technology Centres in Belagavi and Hubballi as the state expands its tech ecosystem beyond Bengaluru.
Karnataka is expanding its technology infrastructure beyond Bengaluru, with the state government approving Global Technology Centres (GTCs) in Belagavi and Hubballi.
The move comes as the state prepares to showcase its growing AI and deeptech ecosystem at Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026.
Announced on September 29, the two GTCs will be established under the Local Economy Accelerator Programme (LEAP), with the government aiming to give local talent, startups and technology-driven enterprises access to infrastructure closer to home.
Two new centres for North Karnataka
The Belagavi GTC will be set up across approximately 10,000 sq ft at Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU), with plug-and-play facilities. The project will cost Rs 82.80 lakh over three years, with Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM) as the implementing agency.
The Hubballi centre will also cover around 10,000 sq ft at the Hubballi IT Park, on rent-free premises. It will involve Rs 5.80 crore in expenditure over three years, including Rs 4.90 crore in capital expenditure and Rs 90 lakh in operational expenditure.
KDEM will implement the Hubballi project, while Karnataka Rural Infrastructure Development Limited (KRIDL) will undertake the infrastructure development.
Both centres will be funded through LEAP's allocation for creating incubators and accelerators. The programme has a total allocation of Rs 1,000 crore over five years, with Rs 200 crore approved for the first year and Rs 110 crore earmarked for incubators and accelerators.
The 2025-26 state Budget had already announced GTCs through Karnataka State Electronics Development Corporation (KEONICS) in Mangaluru, Hubballi and Belagavi, with plug-and-play facilities.
The government says the centres will strengthen links between educational institutions, startups, technology companies and industry while creating opportunities for local talent and technology enterprises.
AI and robotics take centre stage at BTS 2026
The move comes as Karnataka prepares for the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit, scheduled for November 17–19 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre under the theme ‘AI & Beyond’.
A dedicated AI and Robotics Pavilion will span more than 50,000 sq ft and is expected to bring together nearly 101 robotics and drone startups. The pavilion will feature humanoid robots, quadruped racing, autonomous systems, warehouse drones, industrial AI robots and an AI Digital Twin Simulator of Bengaluru.
The space will also include live demonstration zones, startup exhibits, a robotics racing arena, research displays and a pitchathon stage. The focus will be on technologies that take AI beyond software and into physical systems that can perceive, process information, navigate and act.
BTS 2026 is expected to bring together more than 1,800 exhibitors, 1,000 technology startups and 25,000 delegates from India and overseas.
Together, the GTCs and the summit reflect two parts of Karnataka's technology push: building infrastructure and startup ecosystems outside Bengaluru while continuing to position the state capital as a meeting point for emerging technologies and global investment.

articles.title: Chrome, Firefox Updates Patch Over 100 Vulnerabilities
articles.text:
Google and Mozilla on Tuesday announced fresh Chrome and Firefox updates that address over 100 vulnerabilities.
The latest Chrome release was rolled out with fixes for 32 security defects, including a critical-severity buffer overflow issue in ANGLE tracked as CVE-2026-102331 and reported by an external researcher.
Google addressed 25 high-severity security weaknesses, most of which are uninitialized resource and use-after-free vulnerabilities. It also resolved five high-severity type confusion flaws in the V8 JavaScript and WebAssembly engine.
The browser update also fixes high-severity improper privilege management, UI misconfiguration, out-of-bounds read/write, cross-site scripting (XSS), and buffer overflow issues.
External researchers reported 15 of the patched security holes, but Google has not disclosed the bounty rewards paid for 14 of them. According to its advisory, the company handed out $1,000 for a low-severity missing authorization bug in Payments.
The latest Chrome iteration is now rolling out to users as versions 154.0.8037.92/.93 for Windows and macOS, and as version 154.0.8037.92 for Linux.
Mozilla released Firefox 157 with patches for approximately 76 vulnerabilities, including 38 high-severity security defects, mostly use-after-free and sandbox escape bugs.
The fresh Firefox update also resolves high-severity incorrect boundary conditions, uninitialized memory, privilege escalation, information disclosure, invalid pointer, and JIT miscompilation issues.
Many of the vulnerabilities resolved in Firefox 157 were also fixed in Firefox ESR 153.4, 140.17, and 115.42.
Google and Mozilla make no mention of any of these security defects being exploited in the wild, but users are advised to update their browsers as soon as possible.

articles.title: So what's happening with Russia's new, long-delayed crewed spacecraft?
articles.text:
In what seems like an alternate universe in hindsight, Russia and the European Space Agency began discussing collaboration on next-generation crewed spacecraft two decades ago. Under the agreement, Europe would have provided a service module to power a crew capsule carrying up to six passengers.
Europe ultimately decided not to pursue a crewed spacecraft project at the time, and Russia’s state-backed space corporation, Roscosmos, chose to move ahead with a crewed spacecraft on its own. This project—always seemingly more of a Potemkin village than an effort encompassing real hardware—has gone under various guises over the years:
- PPTS (Perspektivnaya Pilotiruemaya Transportnaya Sistema / Prospective Piloted Transport System): The initial conceptual project name used in 2009
- PTK NP (Pilotiruyemy Transportny Korabl Novogo Pokoleniya / New Generation Piloted Transport Ship): The official technical designation used until 2016
- Federatsiya (Federation): The official name chosen following a public contest and announced in January 2016
- Orel / Oryol (Eagle): A new name adopted in September 2019 when Roscosmos was under the control of Dmitry Rogozin
Actual hardware tests, maybe?
Beyond the name changes and a flood of renderings, after nearly 20 years of work, then, is anything actually happening with the Eagle spacecraft?
For starters, the relatively new chief executive of Roscosmos, Dmitry Bakanov, appears to have jettisoned the “Eagle” name of the spacecraft favored by Rogozin. In a recently published Interfax story, the spacecraft is referred to as PTK NP.

articles.title: La UE despliega su estrategia de IA en América Latina en medio de la disputa global con EEUU y China: el rol de Argentina
articles.text:
La Unión Europea eligió la provincia de Córdoba para desplegar uno de los movimientos más concretos de su estrategia tecnológica en América Latina: la semana pasada, mientras Javier Milei brindaba su discurso ante la Asamblea General de la ONU en contra de las regulaciones a las empresas de IA, la Argentina oficializó su integración a la Red UE-ALC de Supercomputación para Inteligencia Artificial, que busca conectar a centros de ambos continentes, potenciar la soberanía digital y minimizar los riesgos. Esta red entra en funcionamiento en medio de la disputa global con EEUU y China por la infraestructura.
De manera oficial, la iniciativa busca impulsar investigación conjunta en inteligencia artificial, cambio climático, salud y modelos de lenguaje adaptados a idiomas regionales, y prevé la inversión de tres millones de euros ampliables a seis millones, coordinada por el Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC) junto a Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, México, Brasil y Uruguay. Del lado europeo participan España, Portugal, Francia, Italia, Alemania, Eslovenia y Finlandia.
PUBLICIDAD
El anuncio se inscribe en el Global Gateway, la estrategia europea de inversión en infraestructura lanzada en 2021 como contrapeso al avance de China. Y parte de una premisa: sin capacidad propia de cómputo, los países de la región “dependen de soluciones externas”, en referencia al debate sobre soberanía digital frente a la presencia de China y Estados Unidos en la provisión de infraestructura de inteligencia artificial en América Latina. La semana pasada, ambos países acordaron crear un “canal bilateral de comunicación” para incidentes relacionados con la IA, tras la cumbre entre el presidente estadounidense Donald Trump y el líder chino Xi Jinping.
Desde la sede de Bruselas, y ante la consulta de Infobae, funcionarios de la Unión Europea remarcaron que la Alianza Digital UE-ALC plantea “un modelo de transformación digital alternativo, basado en valores comunes”, diferenciado del modelo estadounidense —al que caracterizan como market-driven— y del modelo chino —al que definen como State-driven—. “La Alianza Digital es una asociación digital birregional que impulsa la transformación digital centrada en el ser humano, y apuesta por trabajar en intereses compartidos y promocionar estándares basados en los derechos fundamentales”, agregaron.
PUBLICIDAD
Unas semanas antes del anuncio en Córdoba, la presidenta de la Comisión Europea, Ursula von der Leyen, advirtió ante el Parlamento Europeo en Estrasburgo que el déficit comercial con China había llegado a un punto de inflexión. “Algunos dicen que el segundo shock chino se avecina, pero ya está aquí”, afirmó en su discurso sobre el Estado de la Unión el 16 de septiembre, con una advertencia sobre la dependencia europea en materias primas críticas —superior al 80% para muchos insumos y al 90% en algunas tierras raras— y un llamado a “usar todas las herramientas a disposición para reequilibrar la relación”.
En el mismo discurso, defendió la Ley de Inteligencia Artificial (AI Act), la primera regulación integral del mundo aprobada para establecer un marco legal común y seguro. “Queremos IA con agencia humana. Esta es la esencia del camino europeo”, sostuvo von der Leyen.
PUBLICIDAD
Este posicionamiento europeo choca, por lo menos en el plano discursivo, con una línea que Javier Milei viene planteando desde enero de este año. En el Foro Económico Mundial de Davos, el presidente fue categórico: “Lo más responsable que pueden hacer los estados respecto al tema es dejar de fastidiar a quienes están creando un mundo mejor”, y descartó los escenarios de riesgo como “una tontería”.
En junio, Milei fue un paso más allá y publicó una columna en el Financial Times proponiendo la creación de “corporaciones no humanas” con responsabilidad limitada que operarían en mercados globales sin sujetarse a marcos nacionales de rendición de cuentas —una propuesta que generó debate legal inmediato y que va mucho más allá de simplemente no regular.
PUBLICIDAD
El 23 de septiembre, Milei llevó esa postura ante los jefes de Estado reunidos en la ONU y prometió que Argentina no regulará de manera preventiva la inteligencia artificial. “Queremos ser el lugar más competitivo del mundo para desarrollarla, con el compromiso de no regular de manera preventiva”, afirmó.
Argentina figura entre los países de la región con menor desarrollo de una regulación específica sobre inteligencia artificial. Aunque existen proyectos legislativos y lineamientos para el uso de estas herramientas en el sector público, el país todavía no cuenta con una ley nacional integral que establezca obligaciones generales para desarrolladores, empresas y organismos estatales. En contraste con Perú, que ya tiene una norma reglamentada, y con Brasil, Chile y Colombia, que avanzan en marcos basados en riesgos, transparencia y supervisión humana, y con las directrices de la Unión Europea, la regulación argentina permanece fragmentada y sin una autoridad específica de aplicación.
PUBLICIDAD
En términos concretos, la participación en la Red UE-ALC -en un principio hasta 2028- no obliga al país a adoptar ningún reglamento sobre IA. La Secretaria de Innovación, Ciencia y Tecnología, Adriana Baravalle, participó del panel sobre la red en el marco de CARLA, junto al embajador de la Unión Europea en Argentina, Erik Høeg, y representantes de centros de supercomputación de América Latina, el Caribe y Europa.
Según el comunicado oficial, en el encuentro se analizaron “oportunidades para ampliar la cooperación, fortalecer capacidades tecnológicas y potenciar el uso de infraestructura avanzada para la investigación, la innovación y el desarrollo productivo”.
PUBLICIDAD
Clementina como nodos de referencia
Además de integrar la red, Argentina figura como uno de los nodos centrales del proyecto a través de la supercomputadora argentina, Clementina. Esta integración tiene como antecedente el proyecto RISC2, financiado por la UE entre 2021 y 2023, del que Argentina ya formaba parte.
“Con la creación de la Red de Supercomputo UE-ALC, Argentina manifestó su interés en participar en la nueva Red a través de Clementina XXI. Este interés se formalizó durante el Global Gateway Forum, celebrado en Bruselas en octubre de 2025, con la adopción de la declaración conjunta de interés. La Red de Supercomputo contempla una serie de actividades y paquetes de trabajo”, remarcaron desde Bruselas.
PUBLICIDAD
En cuanto al acceso concreto a infraestructura europea, la UE informó a Infobae que los investigadores argentinos deberán participar en una convocatoria abierta —que se publicará en los próximos meses— con criterios objetivos de selección para los casos de uso conjunto. No hay una asignación presupuestaria nacional para cada país: la participación argentina se canalizará a través de actividades como intercambios de movilidad, formación, escuelas de verano y financiamiento de investigadores en proyectos regionales.
Según supo este medio, todas las actividades previstas para la primera etapa de la red están financiadas con el aporte europeo, aunque Brasil se comprometió a destinar ocho millones de euros, equivalentes a 50 millones de reales, para fortalecer la cooperación en computación de alto rendimiento dentro de la región, con Europa y con África, ejecución que permanece suspendida a la espera del resultado de las próximas elecciones.

articles.title: Trump unveils voluntary AI safety pact, backs more data centers, and officially renames AI "Super Intelligence"
articles.text:
What just happened? Donald Trump has announced that the CEOs of the biggest tech and AI companies in the US have signed a "morally binding" agreement to establish controls on artificial intelligence. The president used the announcement to reiterate his support for data centers, too, claiming tech companies will make communities "happy" about their construction. He also signed an executive order renaming artificial intelligence to "superintelligence."
After a meeting with executives that included SpaceX's Elon Musk, OpenAI's Greg Brockman, Anthropic's Dario Amodei, Meta's Mark Zuckerberg, Google's Sundar Pichai and Nvidia's Jensen Huang, Trump announced the Joint Commitment On Frontier Responsibilities.
Under the agreement, which Trump posted to his Truth Social platform, companies agree to have robust internal processes and controls to ensure their technology behaves as intended, and that any issues are promptly resolved. They are also asked to partner with external auditors to ensure the controls, monitoring and detection are working as intended and that their models do not "hack or access technical systems in unintended ways."
Trump added that a board would be created to oversee the safety of AI tools, though he never said who would be appointed.
"It's almost like a constitution, in a way," Trump said. "And the biggest people in the world signed that, and I signed it as president."
The agreement appears completely voluntary; there's no mention of any repercussions should a company fail to live up to the "morally binding" deal. It also appears that companies can choose their own evaluators and aren't compelled to make their findings public.
Trump also doubled down on his support for data center construction. "These big, powerful, very rich, very smart companies are going to be making massive contributions to communities," Trump told reporters. He previously said those protesting the facilities were "making a mistake." The president also said the only reason communities should oppose data centers is if they want to "end up being backwards and poor."
Credit: Bloomberg
Something else Trump reiterated was his previous call to rename artificial intelligence "Super Intelligence." Trump signed an executive order instructing US government departments and agencies to start using the term, or "SI," when referring to the technology. The order said SI will take the place of AI in "official correspondence," websites, reports and other forms of communication.
"As these capabilities continue to improve, they increasingly represent not merely artificial intelligence, but a new era of Super Intelligence," the order said. Trump previously said the word "artificial" made the technology sound "fake."
Some tech bosses, including Musk and Zuckerberg, have started using the term, but it seems extremely unlikely that the public will do the same.
After the agreement was announced, Zuckerberg said that it was created to assure the American public that their technology was trustworthy.
How much impact the Joint Commitment On Frontier Responsibilities has on the industry remains to be seen. Following a series of AI agents from different companies going rogue, several firms have announced new safety measures and a pause in frontier model training. Moreover, some of the safeguards in the agreement already exist and have done little to prevent the security incidents.

articles.title: Juíza dos EUA autoriza Paramount a comprar Warner Bros. Discovery
articles.text:
A Paramount recebeu autorização judicial para concluir a aquisição da Warner Bros. Discovery por US$ 110 bilhões (R$ 561 bilhões). A decisão foi emitida nesta quarta-feira (30) pela juíza distrital Araceli Martínez-Olguín, encerrando impasse que se arrastava havia meses nos Estados Unidos.
A magistrada aprovou acordo firmado entre as empresas e uma coalizão de 12 estados estadunidenses liderada pela Califórnia. O grupo havia processado as companhias sob a alegação de que a fusão poderia prejudicar a concorrência nos mercados de cinema e televisão.
Com a aprovação, um dos últimos grandes obstáculos para a conclusão da operação foi removido. A fusão reunirá sob o mesmo grupo importantes estúdios, canais de televisão, serviços de streaming e operações jornalísticas, incluindo Paramount Pictures, Warner Bros., CBS, CNN, HBO Max e Paramount+.
Acordo impõe condições à nova empresa
- Para encerrar a disputa judicial, a Paramount assumiu uma série de compromissos que deverão ser cumpridos após a conclusão da operação;
- Um deles determina que a companhia combinada lance pelo menos 30 filmes por ano nos cinemas dos Estados Unidos durante cinco anos. A partir dos anos seguintes, a exigência poderá chegar a 32 produções anuais;
- A empresa também terá de investir US$ 300 milhões (cerca de R$ 1,5 bilhão) adicionais por ano na produção cinematográfica estadunidense, em compromisso que totaliza pelo menos US$ 1,5 bilhão (aproximadamente R$ 7,7 bilhões) ao longo de cinco anos. O acordo prevê ainda penalidades caso as metas de produção não sejam cumpridas;
- Outro compromisso determina que as negociações de distribuição dos canais básicos de TV a cabo da Paramount e da Warner Bros. sejam realizadas separadamente durante cinco anos;
- A empresa também concordou em manter um serviço gratuito de streaming semelhante ao Pluto TV e preservar seu serviço e qualidade atuais.
Conselho vai supervisionar CBS e CNN
Um dos pontos mais sensíveis do acordo envolve as operações jornalísticas. A Paramount concordou em criar um conselho de independência editorial para supervisionar padrões jornalísticos da CBS News e da CNN. A estrutura terá como objetivo preservar a independência editorial das duas redes após a união das empresas.
O acordo também prevê mecanismos independentes de acompanhamento do cumprimento das obrigações. Um monitor independente e outras estruturas de supervisão deverão verificar se a nova empresa está respeitando os compromissos assumidos.
Leia mais:
- Paramount discute investimento de R$ 8,1 bilhões para salvar megafusão com a Warner
- Paramount fecha acordo e remove principal obstáculo para comprar a Warner por US$ 81 bilhões
- Paramount avalia receber investimento de Elon Musk enquanto se prepara para concluir aquisição da Warner
Estados haviam tentado bloquear a fusão
A decisão desta quarta-feira é resultado de disputa que ganhou força em julho, quando a Califórnia e outros 11 estados entraram com uma ação para impedir a aquisição.
Os estados argumentavam que a operação poderia reduzir a concorrência e afetar trabalhadores e consumidores. Em 21 de setembro, porém, a Paramount e a coalizão chegaram a um acordo que estabeleceu as condições para encerrar o processo.
Entre as medidas acertadas naquela ocasião estavam o aumento da produção cinematográfica nos Estados Unidos, a criação de um fundo de US$ 47,5 milhões (cerca de R$ 242 milhões) para trabalhadores afetados pela fusão e regras para preservar negociações separadas dos canais de TV a cabo.
A Paramount também chegou a um acordo separado com o Sindicato dos Roteiristas da América (WGA, na sigla em inglês). Como parte da resolução, a empresa concordou em pagar US$ 17,5 milhões (cerca de R$ 89 milhões) ao fundo de saúde do sindicato e manter os níveis atuais de funcionários da CBS News por cinco anos.
Uma das maiores fusões de Hollywood
A conclusão da operação vai unir duas das principais estruturas tradicionais do entretenimento estadunidense. De um lado estão marcas, como Paramount Pictures, CBS e Paramount+; do outro, Warner Bros., HBO Max e CNN.
A nova companhia também terá extenso catálogo de filmes e séries e reunirá operações de cinema, televisão, streaming e jornalismo sob o mesmo grupo.
A Paramount anunciou ainda que Ynon Kreiz, CEO da Mattel, será co-CEO da companhia resultante da fusão ao lado de David Ellison. Kreiz ficará responsável pela operação e integração dos negócios, enquanto Ellison continuará concentrado na direção estratégica, tecnologia, relações com talentos e alocação de capital.
Com a autorização judicial, a aquisição de US$ 110 bilhões (R$ 561 bilhões) fica liberada para avançar rumo à conclusão.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Amazon’s delivery driver smart glasses will reportedly take photos ‘almost constantly’
articles.text:
Amazon deliveries could soon come with a new catch: the delivery driver’s smart glasses will be snapping photos of anything they see while they’re in use, including people and private property. Bloomberg reports that the glasses could take “several thousand captures in a single driver’s typical shift,” which Amazon plans to upload to its AI Wellspring platform. When asked if customers will be able to opt-out of this, Amazon’s Viraj Chatterjee told Bloomberg, “We haven’t thought about that.”
Amazon’s delivery driver smart glasses will reportedly take photos ‘almost constantly’
Amazon doesn’t have much to say about privacy when it comes to drivers wearing camera-equipped smart glasses.
Chatterjee claimed Amazon’s only using the data from the glasses to “enhance the delivery process,” adding, “The intent has never been stuff like surveillance.” The impact of surveillance tech won’t be new to Amazon’s delivery drivers, who have had AI cameras watching in their vehicles and complained about it failing to register secured seat belts, or forcing them to pull over to take a sip of coffee, or having footage from the cameras leaked online.
Chatterjee also told Bloomberg that Amazon’s systems will blur any people and license plates in the images before they’re passed along for human review. Bloomberg says Amazon confirmed that “images from the smart glasses could be obtained with a warrant,” but wouldn’t specify how long it plans to store the images for. There reportedly won’t be a way for customers to see any images Amazon has of them or their property, or ask Amazon to delete those photos.
The photos from the glasses will reportedly be of a similar quality to the quick pictures delivery drivers snap when they drop off a package. Amazon says it’s planning to put 20,000 more pairs of the glasses in the field by the end of 2027, and drivers wearing them in a pilot program have already made over 275,000 deliveries.

articles.title: Meta disputes claim that Muse read a user's private messages without permission | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Meta is refuting a journalist’s claim that its AI agent Muse read the user’s private messages without permission. Following an earlier report from Inc. columnist Jason Aten that detailed the issue, Meta VP of Communications Andy Stone pushed back, making it clear that the company does not believe its product did this without the user’s consent.
“The Messages integration in the Muse app for Mac is entirely opt-in,” Stone wrote on X in response to the claims made by the piece. “You have to enable both Full Disk Access and the Messages connector for Muse to be able to read your Messages content. It can’t read your Messages unless you do this.”
Despite Meta’s denial, many people are still suspicious that Meta isn’t being truthful.
That’s not surprising, given the tech giant’s years of mishandling consumer data, which has led to lawsuits, FTC violations, and fines. Just days ago, for instance, a New Mexico jury determined the tech giant had misled users about its data practices in a case that resulted from the 2018 Cambridge Analytica data breach scandal.
Whether users can trust Muse will be a deciding factor in whether or not Meta wins the consumer AI market. Although its app is faring well now, and remains No. 1 on the App Store, Meta’s reputation may not recover if more reports like this emerge, true or not. If anything, the company should be engaging with the journalist directly to determine how this could have possibly happened, instead of just denying that it did.
Stone’s official statement from Meta follows a more technical reply from Meta Superintelligence Labs executive David Singleton, who responded directly to Aten on Threads, explaining that the set of permissions a user must grant to let Muse read their messages on the Mac involves “three separate steps of application-level permissions and built-in macOS system-level protections.” He said these “can’t be circumvented even if the Muse application had a bug.”
The steps involve explicitly choosing to grant Muse Full Disk Access, which would then allow the user to choose what level of access Muse is being granted to the Messages app (i.e., None, Read only, or Read). If Full Disk Access is not enabled, these options are grayed out.
In addition, when allowing Full Disk Access, the dialog invokes the macOS Settings user interface, where the user has to again manually confirm that they intend to take this action. Doing this triggers a full restart of the Muse app, Singleton wrote, which makes it even less likely that such a choice could be made accidentally without the user’s knowledge.
However, Aten’s report claimed that when Muse read his messages, Full Disk Access was off. He also said that when he asked Muse to explain how this occurred, the AI said that it was syncing his “device notifications.” That means, Aten believes, that Muse was passing along the text of his incoming banner notifications on the Mac to the AI agent.
Singleton disputed this, too, saying that the AI was confused and gave an incorrect explanation of what happened. He then pointed to Meta’s page about Muse’s security architecture and bug bounty process.
In short, the company’s response is essentially that what Aten said happened did not and could not have happened.
This is not the only incident where Muse has allegedly overstepped and won’t likely be the last. Another user, YouTuber Matt Robb, recently said that Muse mishandled a task in which he was selling things on Facebook Marketplace, leading to his address being shared and a buyer showing up when he wasn’t even home. Singleton is apparently looking into that one, per his response on Threads, suggesting that the company believes this one, at least, could be its fault.

articles.title: La nouvelle IA de Meta est accusée de lire tous vos messages, même si vous refusez
articles.text:
Le 8 septembre dernier, Meta a déployé aux États-Unis son nouveau modèle baptisé Meta Muse. Ce dernier est capable de répondre à toutes sortes de questions, mais aussi d’interagir avec des applications et d’effectuer des tâches à la place de l’utilisateur, comme réserver un hôtel en ligne.
Meta met particulièrement en avant le respect de la vie privée de sa nouvelle IA, mais la réalité semble quelque peu différente. Récemment, nous apprenions que Meta Muse pouvait déléguer certains appels téléphoniques à un centre d’appel. Aujourd’hui, un journaliste spécialisé dans la tech rapporte que la nouvelle IA de Meta a accédé à ses iMessages alors qu’il le lui avait interdit.
Malgré une interdiction d’accès, Meta Muse utilise des messages personnels pour répondre à une requête
Tout commence lorsque Jason Aten, chroniqueur et journaliste tech pour le média américain Inc., décide d’installer le modèle Meta Muse sur son iPhone et son Mac afin de le tester. Dans un premier temps, il demande à l’intelligence artificielle d’écrire une courte biographie à son sujet et de l’aider dans son travail, notamment en lui proposant des idées de personnes à interviewer et des sujets à traiter. Jusqu’ici, tout se passe normalement. Mais à un certain moment, Meta Muse lui suggère qu’une conversation en cours entre Jason et son co-animateur de podcast au sujet des nouveaux iPhones pourrait faire l’objet d’un article. Cette notification fait par ailleurs référence à une autre conversation avec son rédacteur en chef concernant la préparation d’une chronique.
Selon toute vraisemblance, Meta Muse a donc eu accès aux conversations personnelles de Jason Aten. Le problème ici n’est pas que l’IA se réfère à des messages, mais qu’elle le fasse alors que le journaliste lui ait interdit l’accès lors de sa configuration. En effet, Jason Aten l’affirme : « je me souviens avoir explicitement choisi de ne pas lui permettre d’accéder à mes messages, à mon calendrier et à mes autres informations personnelles ».
Meta Muse réfute en bloc avoir un accès à l’historique des messages du journaliste
Le journaliste a demandé à Meta Muse s’il avait accédé à son historique de messages malgré son interdiction, ce que l’intelligence artificielle a formellement réfuté. Cette dernière a expliqué avoir seulement eu accès au texte affiché sur les bannières de notification. Peu convaincu par cette explication, Jason Aten a mené sa propre enquête. Il affirme avoir constaté que Muse synchronisait des données issues de la base de données locale de l’application Messages sur son Mac. Et le journaliste ne cache pas son mécontentement : « Fouiller dans la base de données privée de mes messages sur mon Mac ne me rassure pas du tout. Mentir à ce sujet n’est pas mieux ».
Cet épisode nous rappelle donc que l’IA a tendance à se montrer particulièrement intrusive, même lorsque nous lui interdisons de mettre son nez dans certaines affaires.
